Hamas has agreed to disarm. Israel should now agree to peace
items.description: Cover image: picture alliance / ASSOCIATED PRESS | Abdel Kareem Hana At the end of July, Hamas agreed to a Board of Peace (BoP) roadmap to implement Phase 2 of the three-stage ceasefire agreement. At its core is Hamas’s willingness to decommission its weapons. This would have been unthinkable only a few years ago and offers a realistic pathway for ending the Islamist group’s governance and security control over the devastated Strip. This process will only begin once Israel has fully complied with its Phase 1 obligations , which it has yet to do. More fundamentally, it will require Israel to accept a process to end its military presence in Gaza and ultimately engage in negotiations towards Palestinian self-determination. Netanyahu and his hardline government have rejected the roadmap out of hand and are now the main threat to the ceasefire deal. Having been largely sidelined, Europe now has a role to play in ensuring the deal succeeds. The unfinished phase 1 Announced in September 2025, Trump’s 20-point plan aims to end the war in Gaza in three phases. The first phase conditioned the full cessation of hostilities and emergency relief on the release of Israeli hostages held by Palestinian groups. The second phase aims to remove Hamas from power and begin reconstruction—the roadmap Hamas agreed to in July outlines how this stage will work. The final phase would end with Israel’s full withdrawal from Gaza, the return of the Palestinian Authority (PA) and the launch of a “credible pathway to Palestinian self-determination and statehood”. So far, the plan has significantly reduced violence, secured the return of all Israeli hostages held by Palestinian factions and prompted a partial redeployment of Israeli military forces. However, in violation of the agreement, Israel has continued to strike civilians and militants in Gaza , and impede the entry of humanitarian aid. The Israeli military has also advanced beyond the Yellow Line , to which it was supposed to withdraw in the first phase. At the same time, Israel has continued to demolish Palestinian homes and infrastructure in the 70% of Gaza that remains under its control. Israel may now be seeking to create a new de facto border with Gaza and effectively annex a large chunk of the territory, potentially preparing for the return of Israeli settlements there in the future. The roadmap Once Phase 1 is complete, Palestinian factions will begin handing over their heavy weapons to the Palestinian National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG), a transitional body created as part of the 20-point plan to replace Hamas governance and security control in the Strip. This will include the full alphabet soup of Palestinian armed groups —many of which are more hardline than Hamas—as well as Israeli-backed militias . Heavy weapons will effectively be placed under lock and key, monitored by the International Stabilisation Force (ISF), which will deploy as a buffer between Israeli forces and NCAG-controlled areas. BoP officials have said Palestinian weapons could ultimately be dismantled and melted down . This would replicate how Northern Ireland’s decommissioning process dealt with weapons held by paramilitary groups. Tunnels and weapons production facilities would also be put out of action. Small arms like AK-47s will instead be regulated by NCAG through a system of permits. NCAG will also establish a new police force made up of newly trained recruits and members of the Hamas-run civil police vetted and approved by the BoP. Critically, the roadmap links the decommissioning process “to an Israeli withdrawal, in phases, from the areas under its control in Gaza”. According to previous understandings, Israel would withdraw to a new “Red Line” by the end of Phase 2, and from there to a “Black Line” along Gaza’s perimeter, where it would retain a narrow buffer zone until “Gaza is properly secure from any resurgent terror threat.” While the contours of Phase 2 are now clear, the final operational details still need to be hammered out between the sides during follow-up talks. Questions also remain over the lack of funding for the NCAG and the status of the ISF, which to date has only around 200 pledged troops from Morocco, though smaller numbers may also come from countries including Kosovo and Uganda. Meanwhile, the new Palestinian police force has yet to begin training in Egypt. Europe is right to avoid directly funding the BoP. But it has considerable expertise in disarmament and security-sector reform, including through the EU’s EUPOL COPPS mission , which was established to assist the PA police in the West Bank. Europeans should offer critical personnel and technical expertise to support both the decommissioning process and the training of the new Palestinian police force. The spoiler The biggest obstacle remains Israel’s opposition to any transitional political process that would eventually force it out of the Strip and into talks on Palestinian self-determination The biggest obstacle remains Israel’s opposition to any transitional political process that would eventually force it out of the Strip and into talks on Palestinian self-determination. The Israeli government has instead vowed to remain in Gaza and continue its military attacks. It has also opposed NCAG taking over until Hamas fully disarms, and demanded the right to veto troop contributions to the ISF from “ hostile ” countries such as Turkey and Qatar. BoP officials now appear to be altering parts of the laboriously negotiated deal (and its own press release ) to accommodate Israel’s hardline stance. They now state that Israeli withdrawal beyond the Yellow Line would begin only once the decommissioning process is complete. This appears to contradict the original text and Nikolay Mladenov, the BoP’s high representative, who initially said the two would move forward “ in lockstep ”. The accompanying Explanatory Note also reinforces this interpretation, outlining “a step-by-step process linking withdrawal phases to verified decommissioning steps.” Such manoeuvring risks undermining Hamas support for the agreement. Moreover, by conditioning all further Israeli withdrawals on Gaza’s full demilitarisation, the BoP is in effect giving Israel a veto over the process itself, allowing it to deepen its control over the eastern half of Gaza. Given the near impossibility of removing every single Palestinian weapon, as many are held by families, clans, criminal networks and jihadi groups, Israel could argue indefinitely that the conditions for its withdrawal have not been met. But even BoP efforts to placate Israel have failed to satisfy prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu. He continues to demand that the deal be re-negotiated, insisting that no Israeli redeployment will take place, even to the original Yellow Line, until Hamas has fully disarmed. The path forward Having secured Hamas’s unprecedented agreement to decommission its weapons, the BoP now needs to show the political will to implement its own deal. US officials have already warned Israel that US president Donald Trump would be “ very, very disappointed ” if Netanyahu derailed it. Although the prime minister’s far-right coalition limits his room for manoeuvre, Netanyahu has invested heavily in portraying his close relationship with Trump as a political asset—which means he cannot easily afford a public rupture with him. Mladenov has won wide international praise for brokering the deal. Rather than modifying the terms he himself negotiated and risk the diplomatic gains already achieved, he should use his current political capital and Trump’s momentary re-engagement to insist that Israel implements rather than rewrites the agreement. If necessary, he should be prepared to call out Israeli obstruction, just as he previously cast Hamas as the main obstacle. Europe can further strengthen his hand by also highlighting Israel’s non-compliance with its obligations, as the Arab and Turkish mediators have done . The EU should also resume discussions on suspending the Association Agreement with Israel unless it complies. Sustained diplomatic engagement before Israel’s October elections should aim to shift the terms of the domestic debate. The Israeli opposition has also been critical of the deal, accusing Netanyahu of weakness by allowing Hamas to survive, and is unlikely to chart a radical new course on Gaza if it wins. Nevertheless, opposition figures have also acknowledged that Israel’s battlefield gains need to be converted into lasting diplomatic achievements. Europe should use the political framework established by the Gaza roadmap to reinforce this logic and demonstrate how military gains can be converted into a sustainable political settlement. Ultimately, success will depend on whether both sides conclude that diplomacy offers greater rewards than renewed war. Hamas is unlikely to complete decommissioning unless it believes that concessions today will lead to genuine political gains tomorrow towards Palestinian liberation. Equally, Israel will only embrace a durable ceasefire if it sees political transformation within Hamas that locks it into credible peace negotiations as a means of strengthening its long-term security. This makes Phase 3 every bit as important as Phase 2. Without a credible pathway towards Palestinian self-determination, decommissioning risks becoming an end in itself rather than the foundation of a lasting Israeli-Palestinian peace. Equally, a future Israeli government will need to view full implementation of the Gaza agreement not as a concession to Hamas, but as the indispensable stepping stone towards normalisation with Saudi Arabia and deeper integration with the Arab and Islamic world. Europe should therefore work with its Arab partners to ensure that the Gaza deal is tied to a regional package. That would allow a future Israeli government to present withdrawal from Gaza and acceptance of a political process leading to a two-state solution not as unilateral compromises, but as part of a US-brokered grand bargain that underpins Israeli integration and security in the region. items.title: Trust the numbers: Germans are open to a more hawkish China policy
items.description: Reluctance among German decision-makers has long stopped Berlin taking a tougher economic approach towards China. When France, Italy, Lithuania, the Netherlands and Spain recently pressed the European Commission for tougher measures and faster trade defence action against China, Germany not only declined to join, it even called for stronger industrial ties with Beijing. Yet, one thing Berlin should not worry about is voters’ disapproval should it pursue a more hawkish China policy. ECFR polling data find that Germans are the most China-sceptical out of 15 European countries surveyed. No fewer than 60% of Christian Democrat and Social Democrat supporters regard the country as an adversary or rival. In contrast, elsewhere in Europe, majorities still see China as either a “necessary partner” or even an ally. In Italy and Spain, 56% and 65% of people hold this view respectively. (Closest to the sceptical Germans are the French public; President Emmanuel Macron’s increasingly hawkish political posture vis-à-vis Beijing may have found an audience willing to listen.) The China shock has hit Germany particularly hard: its manufacturing sector lost around 420,000 jobs between 2019 and 2025 and it continues to shed 10,000 jobs each month. The car industry is paying the highest costs , being squeezed out of a market increasingly dominated by Chinese manufacturers at home and abroad. The mood in the European Council is shifting, and with Germany’s acquiescence. When EU leaders met in June 2026, they backed a stronger trade defence toolbox of existing measures against China. This included instruments such as the Industrial Accelerator Act’s “Buy European” provisions and limits on high-risk Chinese technology. Despite its past hesitations, Germany no longer acts as a spoiler on firmer EU action, and it has cautiously supported this new direction. Nevertheless, the combination of growing public scepticism towards China, mounting pressure on German industry and appetite for a more assertive policy on the European level creates a political mandate that German decision-makers could yet seize. The German public’s views on the energy transition should also prove encouraging for their leaders. Voters want to see investment in renewables: 57% back what would amount to the growing electrification of the economy. Across the countries polled by ECFR, 61% of respondents say they support prioritising renewables and the clean tech sector. This public support should help persuade leaders, including in Germany, that they can take action to limit emerging dependencies on China. They can accelerate the energy transition while de-risking the clean tech sector through providing support for domestic European industries, from wind to batteries. For Berlin, and capitals across Europe, it is safer to move ahead rather than delay. Chinese economic policy is already doing irreparable damage to European industry—but European policymakers still need to protect an increasingly electrified economy from weaponisation by China. If they fail to do so, governments will almost certainly pay the price at the ballot box. Those that pursue electrification and economic de-risking as a single package are most likely to reap the political rewards. Source

items.title: Gourma : La campagne de riposte contre la rougeole-rubéole se déroule dans de bonnes conditions au CM du secteur 11
items.description: BURKINA-GOULMOU-GOURMA-SANTÉ-VACCINATION Gourma : La campagne de riposte contre la rougeole-rubéole se déroule dans de bonnes conditions au CM du secteur 11 Fada N'Gourma, 5 août 2026 (AIB)-La campagne de vaccination de riposte contre la rougeole-rubéole, en cours depuis le 3 août et prévue jusqu'au 9 août 2026, connaît un bon déroulement dans l'aire sanitaire du Centre médical (CM) du secteur 11 de Fada N'Gourma, malgré quelques cas de réticence constatés au lancement de l'opération. Selon le médecin responsable du Centre médical du secteur 11 de Fada N'Gourma, Dr M. Yolande Napon, cette campagne intervient en réponse à une recrudescence des cas suspects de rougeole observée ces derniers mois dans l'aire sanitaire. « Nous avons constaté que plusieurs patients arrivaient avec des signes évocateurs de la rougeole, notamment des conjonctivites et des rhumes. Face à la fréquence des cas notifiés, le gouvernement a pris l'initiative d'organiser cette campagne afin de réduire cette pathologie », a-t-elle expliqué. Le médecin responsable a indiqué que les premiers jours de la campagne ont été marqués par une certaine réticence de la population. Toutefois, grâce aux actions de sensibilisation menées par les équipes de santé et aux différents canaux de communication, l'adhésion des communautés s'améliore progressivement. « Nous sommes allés expliquer aux populations l'importance de la vaccination et nous pensons que les résultats des derniers jours seront meilleurs que ceux du début de la campagne », a-t-elle affirmé. Dr M. Yolande Napon a par ailleurs rassuré que tous les intrants nécessaires à la vaccination sont disponibles et que les équipes sont entièrement mobilisées pour assurer le bon déroulement de l'opération. « Nous avons reçu les vaccins, les seringues et tout le matériel nécessaire. Les agents sont déjà sur le terrain pour administrer les vaccins », a-t-elle précisé. Elle a lancé un appel aux parents et aux leaders communautaires afin qu'ils accompagnent les équipes de santé dans cette opération. « J'invite les parents à faire vacciner leurs enfants et je demande aux leaders communautaires de poursuivre la sensibilisation afin que toute la population adhère à cette campagne », a-t-elle exhorté. Pour cette campagne de riposte, la cible vaccinale a été exceptionnellement élargie aux enfants âgés de 6 mois à 10 ans, alors que la vaccination de routine contre la rougeole concerne habituellement les enfants de 9 à 23 mois. La campagne, qui s'achèvera le 9 août 2026, vise à renforcer l'immunité des enfants afin de freiner la propagation de la maladie dans l'aire sanitaire du Centre médical du secteur 11 de Fada N'Gourma. Agence d’information du Burkina KAC/HB/OO

items.title: Namentenga/ Montée des couleurs : Le Haut- commissaire salue le soutien de la FEME aux appelés de l’IPO
items.description: BURKINA-NAMENTENGA–MONTEE- COULEURS Namentenga/ Montée des couleurs : Le Haut- commissaire salue le soutien de la FEME aux appelés de l’IPO Boulsa, 3 août 2026 (AIB) – Le Haut-commissaire de la province du Namentenga, Adama Conseiga a présidé le lundi 3 août 2026, dans l’enceinte du district sanitaire de Boulsa, la cérémonie mensuelle de montée des couleurs. Pour l’occasion, il a salué l’appui financier de la Fédération des Églises et Missions évangéliques (FEME) en faveur des appelés de l’Immersion patriotique obligatoire (IPO) à Kaya. Fortement mobilisés pour cette cérémonie du premier lundi du mois d’août, les membres des corps constitués ont suivi les interventions du médecin-chef du district sanitaire de Boulsa, Dr Emile Compaoré, et du Haut-commissaire Adama Conseiga. Au cours de la rencontre, la Fédération des églises et missions évangéliques (FEME) a remis une contribution financière de 50 000 FCFA destinée aux jeunes de la province engagés dans l’Immersion patriotique obligatoire à Kaya. Le Haut-commissaire a salué ce geste de solidarité et remercié les responsables de la fédération pour leur engagement en faveur de la jeunesse. Dr Compaoré a indiqué que des rumeurs infondées relayées sur les réseaux sociaux au sujet de la campagne de chimio-prévention du paludisme saisonnier, organisée du 23 au 26 juillet 2026, ont compromis l’atteinte des résultats attendus lors du premier passage. De son côté, le directeur provincial en charge de l’Agriculture, Mamadou Sidibé, a alerté sur la présence persistante d’intrants agricoles non homologués sur le marché local, soulignant les risques qu’ils représentent pour la santé humaine, animale et l’environnemental. Face à cette situation, le Haut-commissaire a mis en garde les auteurs de ces pratiques qu’il a qualifiées d’inciviques et préjudiciables à la population. Le directeur provincial de la Jeunesse, des Sports et de l’Emploi, Pengdwendé Joseph Sawadogo, a, pour sa part, invité les participants à prendre part à une séance d’appui-conseil sur le processus de formalisation des unités économiques et des emplois informels, prévue le 6 août 2026 à Boulsa. Adama Conseiga a également invité les populations à accompagner les travaux de construction du mur de clôture du Centre médical avec antenne chirurgicale (CMA) de Boulsa, à se mobiliser davantage lors des prochaines campagnes de chimio-prévention du paludisme saisonnier et à solliciter les services techniques de l’agriculture et de l’élevage pour bénéficier de conseils appropriés. En clôturant la cérémonie, le Haut-commissaire a rendu un vibrant hommage aux Forces de défense et de sécurité ainsi qu’aux Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP), avant d’inviter les membres des corps constitués à les soutenir par leurs prières. Agence d’information du Burkina JBD/no/yos

items.title: Œuvres «contraires aux bonnes mœurs»: l’artiste Kosa Pic risque une interdiction d’exercer
items.description: Le ministère chargé de la Culture a adressé une mise en demeure à l'artiste burkinabè Kosa Pic, lui ordonnant de supprimer immédiatement de toutes les plateformes numériques les contenus liés à sa toute dernière création. Accusé d'«atteinte aux bonnes mœurs», le chanteur s'expose à des sanctions administratives et judiciaires s'il ne se conforme pas à cette injonction. L'artiste-chanteur Issaka Ouédraogo, plus connu sous le nom de scène Kosa Pic (29 ans), est de nouveau dans la ligne de mire du ministère en charge de la Culture. Selon l'Agence d'Information du Burkina (AIB), le département exige le retrait sans délai de l'ensemble de ses dernières publications artistiques, estimées non-conformes aux valeurs morales en vigueur. En cas d'insoumission, le jeune musicien risque une interdiction pure et simple d'exercer le métier d'artiste et d'éventuelles poursuites judiciaires. Révélé au grand public en 2023, Kosa Pic s'est bâti une notoriété controversée en abordant de manière explicite et crue des thématiques liées à la sexualité. Ce style lui a déjà valu plusieurs déboires avec les instances de régulation. En septembre 2024, le Conseil supérieur de la Communication (CSC) avait appelé les médias et les populations à cesser toute diffusion du clip vidéo «Zaaka», dénonçant un contenu aux images «érotiques voire pornographiques» assorti de textes «vulgaires et indécentes». En juillet 2025, à la suite d'un bref séjour en détention préventive lié à la diffusion de ce même clip, l'artiste avait été condamné à une peine de six mois de prison avec sursis et à une amende de 250 000 F CFA, également assortie du sursis. Cette nouvelle sommation du ministère de la Culture marque un durcissement du ton des autorités face aux dérives artistiques jugées indécentes, plaçant désormais Kosa Pic au pied du mur: bifurquer dans sa démarche créative ou voir sa carrière musicale prématurément stoppée. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Œuvres «contraires aux bonnes mœurs»: l’artiste Kosa Pic risque une interdiction d’exercer est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: A Shortage of Weapons Is Shaping the War With Iran
items.description: T he United States is running out of missiles. After five months of war with Iran, stockpiles of long-range weapons are so low, current and former U.S. defense officials told us, that they don’t believe the U.S. has enough to combat a threat in Asia. The remaining supplies, depending on the munition, are as low as 20 percent of what the Pentagon would like to have in hand. And stores of sophisticated interceptor missiles, such as Patriots and Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) missiles, are too depleted to give or sell the weapons to Ukraine or effectively defend against Iran’s launch of ballistic missiles. Even when troops see Iranian missiles approaching, they are forced to decide in a matter of seconds whether to expend a limited number of interceptors or hope for the best, the defense officials told us. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth this week pleaded with Republicans on Capitol Hill for billions of dollars to replenish America’s dangerously depleted stockpiles of missiles and other crucial munitions. Hegseth’s appeal was nakedly partisan—he ignored Democratic lawmakers entirely—but also long overdue. The Pentagon this year has awarded tens of billions of dollars in contracts to replenish those arsenals. But signing contracts is not the same as delivering missiles. Those contracts will produce munitions over the coming years, not the coming months. The Biden and Trump administrations have invested in the defense industrial base to accelerate production, but for crucial systems such as the Patriot, supply is not projected to meet demand until about 2030. Meanwhile, Iran has ramped up production of its offensive drones and ballistic missiles, and enhanced their capabilities. The war is now being shaped as much by industrial supply and logistics as by economic considerations and the politics of the midterms. P resident Trump raged at the assessment his national-security team gave him at Camp David on Friday, which showed that the U.S. military was running low on the munitions that would be necessary for Trump to order an escalation against Iran, a senior administration official familiar with the meeting told us. If the U.S. were to strike, Tehran would likely launch a barrage of missiles and drones against its neighbors in the region and the American bases they host. The president barked at aides and had some pointed words for the Department of Defense’s leadership. (He is not presently considering staff changes, a White House official told us.) Trump has grown frustrated at his inability to escape the stalemate of the war; he’s seething at its toll on the economy and is desperate to move on. [ Read: This may be Trump’s biggest error in the Iran war ] White House aides are concerned that Trump is losing his leverage in the conflict. He has threatened Iran many times but has rarely followed through; Tehran knows that. Tehran also knows that the U.S. is running low on munitions despite what Hegseth and the president say in public. Military leverage depends not simply on the U.S. ability to strike but also on its capacity to defend against Iran’s retaliation. Iran has displayed the confidence to further test the U.S., attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz. The White House has maintained that Iran would soon face an economic situation so dire that the regime would be forced to negotiate, and U.S. intelligence reports suggest that Iran is struggling. But the Trump administration has been surprised at Tehran’s resilience, and is no longer certain that the regime will reach the point where negotiation is its only option. In the five months since the war started, the president has never faced such a weak position. The shortage of interceptors makes escalation dangerous. Nor would expanded strikes guarantee that Tehran will come back to the table. That may leave diplomacy and concessions as the administration’s least risky option. Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio have repeatedly said that Iran will never be allowed to control any part of the Strait of Hormuz. But Trump is now considering a deal that gives Iran some control over maritime traffic. The proposed agreement between Oman and Iran, pending U.S. and Gulf approval, would reopen the strait by establishing a jointly managed framework for commercial shipping. Such a deal would give Iran the oversight of the crucial waterway it feels it has earned from the war, while also honoring Oman’s insistence on preserving freedom of navigation. A merica’s stockpiles have been under strain for years, but became painfully clear after Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022. The U.S. military fired hundreds of missiles, some costing millions each, during the Trump administration’s 53-day campaign last year against the Houthis in Yemen. That was followed by nearly two weeks of U.S. and Israeli attacks on Iran and the interception of Iranian missiles and drones aimed at Israel. During the first 38 days of the Iran war, the U.S. launched thousands of munitions. Hegseth has repeatedly denied any shortage, including to Trump as recently as last week, one U.S. official told us. On Capitol Hill, the defense secretary did not make a compelling case for the funding he wants, particularly to legislators who face tough reelections partly because of the war’s unpopularity. Between American voters’ frustrations with rising gas prices and Hegseth’s mixed messages and past combative relationship with Congress, “there is no good will for the department here,” one congressional aide told us. [ Read: A tragedy in Iran might persuade Hegseth to change course ] Still, Congress is ultimately expected to provide much of the funds the Pentagon says it needs to replenish its stores. But what the U.S. really needs is time. Depending on the weapon, replenishment to pre-war levels could take as long as five years, Mark Cancian, who tracks munitions stockpiles for the Center for Strategic and International Studies in Washington, D.C., told us. Another three years would get stockpiles “to a level where the Joint Staff and U.S. commanders in charge of the Asia Pacific would be comfortable,” Cancian said. In theory, that gives Beijing plenty of time to take advantage of American shortages with, say, an invasion of Taiwan. “Claims of U.S. munition shortages are false” and the amplification of them is irresponsible, Sean Parnell, Pentagon spokesperson, told us in a statement. “We have everything required to strike at the time and place of the President’s choosing.” The problem predates the Trump administration. After the Cold War, the U.S. reduced the number, and slowed the pace of production, of vital munitions, figuring that long bouts of peace between short, conclusive wars would provide plenty of capacity. But the military has been almost constantly engaged somewhere in conflicts led by missile strikes: Libya, Yemen, Syria, Iran, Nigeria. And Russia’s war with Ukraine has been defined by rapid advances in munitions. The Biden administration signed contracts to replenish Kyiv’s weapons but could not keep up with demand, Cancian told us. The U.S. raced to develop cheaper ways to tackle the Iranian-supplied drones that Russia deployed, and has made some progress. But the stores of interceptors such as Patriots and THAADs were rapidly expended. “There are no good alternatives for stopping ballistic missiles,” Cancian told us. “Without these defensive missiles, attacking missiles will land unopposed. That is what is happening in Ukraine.” Before Russia’s invasion, the U.S. produced roughly 300 Patriot missiles a year, half of which went to allies. Production has since doubled, but badly trails wartime demand. Had the Iran war been over in a matter of several weeks, as the administration initially predicted, the U.S. munitions problem would not be so dire. And the problem would be mitigated “if we knew when the war will end,” one defense official told us. “The real problem is that there is no long-term strategy—and we can’t plan around that.” Before the shortages, the U.S. used its technological advantages to shape its strategy. Now the technological advances of its foes—and the strain they have put on U.S. stockpiles—are forcing Washington to reconsider its strategy again, this time without the long-held assumption that U.S. forces would enjoy an advantage in munitions.

items.title: IHC reserves order on pleas against Imran, Bushra’s alleged solitary confinement
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Thursday reserved its order on petitions seeking to declare the alleged solitary confinement of PTI founder Imran Khan and his spouse Bushra Bibi illegal after hearing detailed arguments from both sides. Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro observed that the court would issue an order after examining the record and directed the parties to submit in writing any judgments they wished to rely on. During the hearing, Adiala Jail Superintendent Sajid Baig, Islamabad Advocate General Naveed Hayat Malik and counsel for the petitioners Barrister Salman Safdar appeared before the court. The advocate general argued that the petitions were not maintainable and maintained that neither Imran nor Bushra had been kept in solitary confinement. He said the prison authorities had instead provided them with facilities exceeding those available to B-class prisoners. He submitted that, owing to security considerations arising from Imran’s political profile, he had been housed separately from other inmates, but such arrangements could not be termed solitary confinement. The jail authorities, he added, had complied with previous court directions by providing newspapers, books and other facilities. Justice Soomro questioned the nature of the security arrangements and asked whether Imran had been extended B-class facilities. The advocate general replied that he was receiving facilities even better than those prescribed for B-class prisoners. Superintendent Sajid Baig informed the court that Imran had been provided more than 500 books so far, besides daily newspapers. He said the PTI founder was not confined to a single cell for 24 hours, explaining that he had access to a compound comprising seven cells where he could move freely during the day. He further contended that the concept of solitary confinement required a prisoner to remain locked in a cell continuously, which was not the case. The advocate general further argued that neither any court nor any competent authority had ordered solitary confinement for either Imran Khan or Bushra Bibi, and that the petitioners could not seek relief beyond what was prayed for in their petitions. Barrister Salman Safdar disputed the government’s stance, arguing that his clients were effectively being subjected to prolonged isolation amounting to mental torture. Referring to his meeting with Imran earlier this year on the Supreme Court’s directions, he said his client had complained of deteriorating eyesight, restricted access to lawyers, political colleagues and family members, and an inadequate supply of books. He told the court that despite facing more than 300 criminal cases, Imran had not been allowed regular consultations with his legal team. According to the counsel, a 65-minute meeting arranged in April following the intervention of the IHC chief justice was the first meaningful consultation after several months, during which most of the discussion centred on the alleged mental distress caused by prison conditions. Justice Soomro asked whether the petitioner had supported the allegations through an affidavit. Barrister Safdar replied that he intended to address every aspect of the case through his arguments. The counsel requested the court to appoint a panel of lawyers to inspect prison conditions, allow weekly telephone conversations between Imran Khan and his two sons, facilitate regular meetings with lawyers and family members, and direct the authorities to permit Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi to spend time together in accordance with prison rules. During the proceedings, books sent by Imran’s family for delivery to the prison were produced before the court, prompting Justice Soomro to seek the list of the books. Aleema Khan also addressed the court, alleging that her brother had received only three books since December and had met family members only a handful of times, mostly pursuant to court orders. She urged the court to direct the prison authorities to produce a complete record of meetings. The advocate general objected to the issue of Imran’s eyesight being raised in the present proceedings, arguing that it was outside the scope of the petitions. Justice Soomro, however, remarked that it would have been appropriate had the medical board’s report also been placed before the court. Separately, the Adiala jail superintendent submitted a report denying that Bushra Bibi had been kept in solitary confinement or subjected to discriminatory treatment. The report stated that the practice of solitary confinement had virtually ceased in prisons and that Bushra Bibi was being accommodated separately only because of security concerns arising from her status as the spouse of a former prime minister. It said she had access to a spacious room, a separate courtyard and kitchen, could move freely within the designated area during the day, received regular medical examinations by female prison staff and was allowed to meet Imran Khan every Tuesday in accordance with prison rules. After completion of arguments, Justice Soomro reserved the matter, observing that any judicial precedents relied upon by the parties should be submitted in writing before the court passed its order.

items.title: Diomande joins Real Madrid as club’s most expensive player [Top 5]
items.description: Real Madrid have reached an agreement with RB Leipzig for Ivorian winger Yan Diomande, with the player set to move to the Santiago Bernabéu this summer. According to Marca , both clubs finalised the agreement on Thursday morning, with Diomande already travelling to Madrid to undergo his medical examination. Real Madrid could officially announce the signing on Thursday, with the transfer set to become the most expensive in the club’s history. The Spanish giants are expected to pay €125 million for the 19-year-old, with a further €10m to €15m potentially payable in add-ons. The deal would take Real Madrid’s spending on new arrivals this summer to more than €300 million, with the club also reportedly spending €55 million on Marc Cucurella, €25 million on Carlos Espai and €20 million on Denzel Dumfries. Ibrahima Konaté and Bernardo Silva, meanwhile, joined the club on free transfers. Real Madrid have also generated substantial revenue from player sales, particularly from academy graduates, with total income from such departures reportedly reaching €184.5 million. Diomande’s arrival is not expected to affect Real Madrid’s ongoing negotiations with Brazilian forward Vinicius Junior, according to Marca . Vinicius has entered the final stages of his current contract, which expires at the end of next season, while Arsenal have reportedly shown strong interest in the forward. items.title: Ghana EXIM Bank’s industrialisation strategy takes shape as Northshore Apparel Hub prepares for launch
items.description: Ghana EXIM Bank’s strategy to drive industrial growth, expand exports, and create jobs through targeted investments in key productive sectors is set to gain significant momentum with the commissioning of the Northshore Apparel Hub in Savelugu later this month. The wholly Ghanaian-owned apparel manufacturing facility, developed by Northshore Apparel Ghana Limited with funding support from Ghana EXIM Bank and other partners, is expected to create 3,000 jobs in its first phase and up to 10,000 jobs when fully operational. President John Dramani Mahama will officially commission the facility on August 28, 2026, in a move that industry stakeholders say underscores the growing role of local investment in advancing Ghana’s industrialisation and export agenda. For Ghana EXIM Bank, the project represents more than the opening of a manufacturing plant. It is one of the flagship outcomes of a broader strategy aimed at supporting sectors with high potential for import substitution, export growth, and job creation. Speaking ahead of the inauguration, the Chief Executive of Ghana EXIM Bank, Sylvester Adinam Mensah, said the Bank’s investment in the Northshore Apparel Hub reflects its commitment to building productive industries capable of transforming the Ghanaian economy. “The Northshore Apparel Hub represents the vision of a Ghana that produces, exports and creates opportunities for its people. This investment reflects Ghana EXIM Bank’s commitment to supporting businesses that generate jobs, strengthen local industry and position Ghana as a competitive manufacturing and export destination.” According to him, the project aligns directly with the Bank’s five-year strategic plan, which prioritises investments in rice production, poultry farming, and garment and apparel manufacturing as key drivers of economic transformation. “Our five-year strategic plan prioritises strategic investments in rice production, poultry farming and garment and apparel manufacturing. The opening of the Northshore Apparel Hub is more than the launch of a factory; it is a powerful statement of what Ghana can achieve when local capital is invested in local enterprise.” He noted that the project demonstrates a deliberate effort to deepen local production while creating opportunities for young people across the country. “It is a clear testament to our collective resolve to expand exports, deepen local production and create meaningful employment opportunities for Ghanaian youth. This is the kind of transformative industrial investment that will drive economic growth and strengthen Ghana’s position in regional and global markets.” The project is also being hailed as a major milestone for indigenous manufacturing and industrial development in Northern Ghana. The Chief Executive Officer of Northshore Apparel Ghana Limited, Nurideen Mohammed, described the facility as a strong example of the capacity of Ghanaian-owned businesses to undertake large-scale industrial ventures and compete internationally. “The Northshore Apparel Hub is proof that Ghanaian-owned businesses can undertake large-scale industrial projects capable of competing on the global stage. Our goal is not only to create jobs but also to build a world-class apparel manufacturing ecosystem that serves local and international markets.” He said the company intends to leverage the hub’s production capacity and strategic location to support export growth, transfer skills, and create long-term economic opportunities for thousands of young people. “We believe manufacturing remains one of the strongest pathways to sustainable job creation. Through this investment, we are creating opportunities for thousands of young Ghanaians while helping to position the Northern Region as an emerging industrial hub.” Beyond the immediate employment opportunities, the Northshore Apparel Hub is expected to stimulate economic activity across the apparel value chain, support Ghana’s export ambitions, and contribute to the government’s broader industrialisation and 24-hour economy agenda. Industry observers say the project demonstrates how partnerships between development finance institutions and private Ghanaian enterprises can unlock large-scale investments capable of transforming local economies, creating jobs, and strengthening Ghana’s manufacturing base.

items.title: Africans reject choosing sides as China, US compete for influence – Afrobarometer
items.description: Africans are increasingly rejecting pressure to align with any single global power, preferring strategic engagement with multiple international partners as the world moves towards a more multipolar order, a new Afrobarometer report has revealed. The 2026 African Insights flagship report, titled “Beyond Borders: Citizen Perspectives on a Shifting Global Order,” found that citizens across 38 African countries do not view relations with major powers such as China, the United States, Russia and former colonial powers as a choice between competing sides. Instead, the report indicates that many Africans support maintaining relations with different global actors based on how effectively those partnerships serve national interests. Afrobarometer found that positive views of one major power do not necessarily translate into negative views of another. Citizens who view China favourably are also more likely to hold favourable views of the United States. The report said this reflects a broader preference for nonalignment, allowing African countries to maximise opportunities in an increasingly competitive global environment. Among major international actors assessed, China received the strongest positive ratings, with 62% of respondents describing its economic and political influence as positive. China recorded the highest positive ratings in 27 of the 38 countries surveyed, with its approval levels remaining stable since the 2019/2021 survey period. The United States, however, recorded a decline in positive perceptions, dropping from 59% to 53% across 30 countries. The European Union recorded 50% positive ratings, while former colonial powers stood at 41%. India received a positive rating of 39%. Russia recorded the lowest positive perception among the major powers assessed, with 36% of Africans viewing its influence positively. Although awareness of Russia’s role in Africa has increased, the report found that newly formed opinions have leaned more negative, with negative ratings increasing by six percentage points. “To the extent that there is an emerging winner in the contest for Africans’ allegiance, China appears to be coming out on top, holding steady in popular assessments, while the United States is losing ground and Russia struggles to gain it,” the report stated. However, Afrobarometer stressed that Africans are not seeking to replace one dominant influence with another. The report said citizens are open to partnerships with different countries “depending on the extent to which each is willing to deal with them fairly, support their national interests, and benefit their country.” Africans prefer neutrality on Russia-Ukraine war The report also examined African perspectives on the Russia-Ukraine war and found strong support for neutrality. Among respondents who said they were aware of the conflict — representing 70% of those surveyed across the 38 countries — 72% said their countries should remain neutral rather than support either side. Majorities supported neutrality in 37 of the 38 countries surveyed. Mali was the only exception, with 72% of respondents supporting Russia. Afrobarometer described the position as a calculated form of nonalignment rather than a lack of interest in global affairs. “This is not neutrality born of indifference, but a rational calculation to maximise national interest in an increasingly uncertain era,” the report stated. Demand for greater African voice globally The report also highlighted strong public support for increased African representation in international decision-making. About 71% of Africans surveyed said their countries should have greater influence in global institutions, including the United Nations. Majorities supported this position in all surveyed countries except Angola. Afrobarometer said the finding aligns with the African Union’s campaign for greater representation, including calls for permanent African seats on the UN Security Council. The organisation concluded that Africans are seeking a more balanced global relationship where the continent can engage multiple partners without being forced into rival camps. “Africa’s citizens appear to understand what their leaders are starting to articulate: that global engagement needn’t be a zero-sum game,” the report stated. It added that a multipolar world could provide African countries with opportunities to expand partnerships and advance their national interests.

items.title: Burkina Faso / Gendarmerie nationale : Le colonel Koudbi Florian Théophile Tago prend le commandement de la 3ᵉ Légion
items.description: Le colonel Koudbi Florian Théophile Tago a officiellement pris le commandement de la 3ᵉ Légion de la Gendarmerie nationale. Il a reçu les insignes de commandement des mains du chef d'état-major de la Gendarmerie nationale, ce jeudi 6 août 2026, au camp de Paspanga, à Ouagadougou. En présence de nombreux frères d'armes, de membres de sa famille et de ses proches, le nouvel officier commandant a reçu le bâton de commandement, symbole de ses nouvelles responsabilités. Il est désormais chargé de la coordination des unités de gendarmerie des régions du Kadiogo, de l'Oubri, du Nando et du Nazinon. Tenant le drapeau national en main, symbole de son engagement envers la nation, le nouveau commandant s'est d'abord incliné à la mémoire de ses frères d'armes tombés dans la lutte pour la reconquête du territoire national. Il a affirmé mesurer l'ampleur de la mission qui lui est confiée et s'est engagé à l'accomplir avec fidélité, loyauté et détermination. Le colonel Koudbi Florian Théophile Tago « Je mesure l'honneur qui m'est fait de commander cette Légion, riche de son histoire, de ses traditions et de l'engagement quotidien de ses femmes et de ses hommes. Je connais les sacrifices que vous consentez et les risques que vous acceptez chaque jour pour que notre drapeau continue de flotter sur chaque portion de notre circonscription et même au-delà », a-t-il déclaré, avant de présenter les trois priorités qui guideront son action. Les trois priorités du nouveau commandant La première priorité, qu'il qualifie d'absolue, est la protection des populations. « Notre légitimité réside dans la confiance de nos concitoyens ; notre efficacité se mesurera à leur sentiment de quiétude. C'est pourquoi je vous invite, partout où vous serez appelés à servir, à être un recours et un secours pour les plus faibles, un réconfort pour les victimes, un guide pour les égarés, une force qui rassure plutôt qu'une force qui inquiète, un rempart contre toutes les formes d'insécurité ; bref, une force humaine au service de la nation », a-t-il souligné. Le nouveau commandant de la 3ᵉ légion de la gendarmerie nationale, le colonel Koudbi Florian Théophile Tago, reçoit la charge de son commandement des mains du chef d'État-major de la gendarmerie Sa deuxième priorité est le renforcement de la cohésion. Il a exhorté ses frères d'armes à préserver l'unité au sein de la Gendarmerie nationale, à consolider la coopération avec les autres Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS) ainsi qu'avec les Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP). La troisième priorité est la culture du résultat. « Nous devons toujours nous rappeler que notre institution, notre hiérarchie et les populations attendent de nous des résultats palpables », a-t-il insisté. Plusieurs autorités militaires et civiles ont assisté à la cérémonie de passation de commandement S'adressant enfin aux populations des régions du Kadiogo, de l'Oubri, du Nando et du Nazinon, le colonel Koudbi Florian Théophile Tago les a invitées à continuer de soutenir et de faire confiance aux Forces de défense et de sécurité ainsi qu'aux Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie. « Les portes de la 3ᵉ Légion, votre Légion, vous seront toujours ouvertes », a-t-il assuré. Pour rappel, le colonel Koudbi Florian Théophile Tago succède au colonel Issa Yaguibou, devenu chef d'état-major de la Gendarmerie nationale. Avant sa nomination, il commandait la 1ʳᵉ Légion de la Gendarmerie nationale basée à Kaya. Serge Ika Ki Lefaso.net

items.title: Economic hardship pushing more Africans to consider leaving their countries – Afrobarometer report
items.description: Nearly half of Africans have considered leaving their countries, with economic hardship and the search for employment emerging as the main factors driving the growing interest in migration, a new Afrobarometer report has revealed. The 2026 African Insights flagship report, titled “Beyond Borders: Citizen Perspectives on a Shifting Global Order,” found that 45% of respondents across 38 African countries have thought about moving to another country, including 25% who said they have considered it “a lot.” The report represents a sharp rise in migration aspirations compared to nearly a decade ago. In 31 countries where the same question was asked between 2016 and 2018, the proportion of citizens who seriously considered leaving increased from 18% to 25%. West Africans recorded the highest levels of interest in emigration, with 34% saying they had thought “a lot” about leaving their countries. The report identified The Gambia, Liberia, Guinea-Bissau and Ghana among countries with some of the highest levels of citizens seriously considering migration. More than half of Gambians (53%) and Liberians (51%) said they had seriously considered leaving, followed by Bissau-Guineans (49%) and Ghanaians (44%). According to Afrobarometer, economic concerns are the dominant motivation behind the trend. Among respondents who had considered emigrating, 50% said they would leave in search of work, while 29% cited poverty or economic difficulties as their main reason. Only a small proportion identified other motivations, including education (4%), political factors (3%) and travel opportunities (3%). The report also found that younger and more educated Africans are more likely to consider leaving their countries. Citizens aged between 18 and 35 years were three times more likely than those above 55 years to seriously consider migration, with 32% of young respondents expressing such interest compared to 11% among older citizens. In Ghana, the report indicated that 55% of young people have seriously considered leaving the country. The most educated respondents were also more likely to contemplate migration, with 31% expressing interest compared to 18% among those with the least education. The study further revealed a shift in preferred destinations among potential migrants. The proportion of respondents who preferred moving to another African country declined from 36% in 2016/2018 to 26%, while interest in North America increased from 21% to 28%. Europe remained one of the most preferred destinations, rising slightly from 27% to 29%. “These findings confirm the familiar story that it is the youngest and most educated who are most likely to depart,” the report stated. It added that while many Africans express a desire to leave the continent, official migration patterns show that most people who eventually move remain within Africa. The report also examined attitudes towards immigration, finding that Africans have mixed views about accepting foreigners into their own countries. While 77% of respondents said they would welcome or not mind having immigrants as neighbours, many expressed reservations about admitting foreign job seekers and refugees. About 64% preferred fewer or no job seekers from other countries, while 70% wanted fewer or no refugees admitted. Afrobarometer said the findings highlight the need for governments to address the conditions driving citizens to seek opportunities elsewhere. “Citizens leave when institutions fail them,” the report stated, arguing that migration trends reflect broader questions about economic opportunities, governance and state performance. The organisation said creating sustainable jobs and improving living conditions will be critical if African countries are to become places where citizens choose to build their futures rather than seek opportunities abroad.

items.title: Burkina : Une trentaine de journalistes renforcent leurs compétences face aux discours de haine et à la désinformation
items.description: L’ONG ACRA, en consortium avec l’Université de Milan-Bicocca, a organisé les 4 et 5 août 2026 à Ouagadougou une formation au profit d’une trentaine de journalistes. Pendant deux jours, ces professionnels des médias ont planché sur trois thématiques complémentaires : la vérification des faits, l’utilisation responsable des plateformes numériques, ainsi que la communication non violente et la transformation des conflits. Cette initiative s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet PENSE LIBRE, qui entend outiller les acteurs locaux pour promouvoir le vivre-ensemble. Alors que les réseaux sociaux accentuent la propagation des rumeurs, une trentaine de professionnels des médias ont été formés à Ouagadougou à la double exigence du fact-checking et de la promotion de la cohésion sociale. Louis Modeste Ouédraogo rappellant la lourde responsabilité qui incombe aux journalistes dans un environnement marqué par la rapidité de la circulation de l’information, en particulier sur les réseaux sociaux À l’ouverture des travaux, Louis Modeste Ouédraogo, président du Conseil supérieur de la communication (CSC), a rappelé la lourde responsabilité qui incombe aux journalistes dans un environnement marqué par la rapidité de la circulation de l’information, en particulier sur les réseaux sociaux. Il a insisté sur la nécessité d’informer avec rigueur, de vérifier les sources, de respecter l’éthique et la déontologie, et d’adopter une communication sensible aux tensions potentielles. Louis Modeste Ouédraogo, a également réaffirmé l’engagement du CSC à accompagner les rédactions dans l’amélioration de leurs pratiques, tout en souhaitant que les acquis de la formation soient largement partagés au sein de chaque média. Les médias, acteurs à part entière du changement social Le coordonnateur pays d’ACRA Burkina, Poingar Couldjim Madibé, a rappelé que le projet PENSE LIBRE, mené avec l’Université de Milan-Bicocca, l’Institut des Sciences et Techniques Endogènes Africaines (ISTEA) au Burkina Faso et le Centre de Recherches en Anthropologie et Sciences Humaines (CRASH) au Tchad, vise à renforcer la tolérance et le dialogue interculturel et interreligieux. « Les médias ne doivent pas être de simples relais d’information. Ils sont aussi des acteurs de changement, des éducateurs, des veilleurs citoyens et des partenaires essentiels dans la prévention des conflits », a-t-il souligné. Le représentant de la ministre en charge de la famille appelant les participants à plus de responsabilité dans le rendu de l'information Le représentant de la ministre de la Famille et de la Solidarité, Amidou Koné, responsable technique chargé de la paix et de la cohésion sociale, a abondé dans ce sens en soulignant le rôle central des médias dans la préservation du lien social. Amidou Koné a mis en garde contre les effets délétères des informations non vérifiées ou des propos stigmatisants, qui peuvent exacerber les divisions. À l’inverse, a-t-il poursuivi, une information rigoureuse et respectueuse de la dignité humaine peut rapprocher les communautés et favoriser le dialogue. Le représentant du ministre de la Famille a également salué la forte présence des femmes journalistes, dont la contribution est indispensable à une couverture médiatique équilibrée et sensible aux réalités de toute la société. Enfin, il a rappelé que le ministère agit, via le Secrétariat technique de la promotion de la paix et du vivre-ensemble (ST/PPVIE), pour promouvoir la prévention des conflits et la culture de paix. Poingar Couldjim Madibé, Coordonnateur Pays Acra Burkina s'est dit satisfait de l'issue de la formation Trois communications pour couvrir tous les angles de la lutte contre la désinformation La première session, animée par Jordan Méda, journaliste à Faso Check, a porté sur les techniques de vérification des faits et l’usage de l’intelligence artificielle (IA) dans ce processus. Il a défini les notions de désinformation, mésinformation et malinformation, avant de présenter des méthodes concrètes pour authentifier une information. Jordan Méda a aussi alerté sur les limites de l’IA, invitant les participants à toujours croiser les résultats obtenus avec d’autres sources fiables. Monsieur Meda a enfin rappelé que tous les faits ne sont pas vérifiables, ce qui impose une prudence accrue dans le traitement de l’actualité. La deuxième intervention, confiée à Richard Thiombiano, spécialiste en cohésion sociale, avait pour thème : « Médias, cohésion sociale et prévention de l’extrémisme violent : quelle responsabilité pour les communicateurs à l’ère de la désinformation et de l’IA ? ». Il a montré comment déconstruire les contre-récits et valoriser les initiatives locales de paix, tout en outillant les journalistes sur les bonnes pratiques en matière de communication de crise. Amélie Judith Nacoulma jugeant l’initiative « venue à point nommé » au regard du contexte national Enfin, Abdoulaye Dao, directeur général de la publicité et de l’observation des contenus (DGPOC), a animé une communication sur le cadre réglementaire de la lutte contre la désinformation et les discours de haine. Il a invité les professionnels à privilégier des discours constructifs et a passé en revue les dispositions du Code pénal applicables à la diffamation, selon sa gravité. L'avis des participants… À l’issue de la formation, organisateurs et participants ont exprimé leur satisfaction. Amélie Judith Nacoulma, responsable des programmes à la radio Ave Maria, a jugé l’initiative « venue à point nommé » au regard du contexte national. Elle a souligné l’utilité des éclairages reçus sur la désinformation et la malinformation, et s’est engagée à transmettre ces connaissances à ses collègues restés en rédaction, en particulier sur les sujets religieux qu’elle traite fréquemment. Un aperçu de la formation François Yogo, journaliste à Canal 3 Burkina, a également salué la formation, qu’il attendait avec impatience. Il a mis en avant l’importance du fact-checking à l’ère de l’IA et s’est dit ravi d’avoir pu approfondir les règles et outils nécessaires. Il a encouragé les organisateurs à multiplier ce type d’initiatives, essentielles pour permettre aux journalistes de traiter l’information dans des conditions optimales. Chaque participant a reçu une attestation de fin de formation. Présente au Burkina Faso depuis une vingtaine d’années, l’ONG ACRA poursuit ainsi son action en faveur de la paix et du vivre-ensemble dans la sous-région. L’objectif affiché est que les journalistes formés deviennent à leur tour des relais, en partageant leurs acquis au sein de leurs rédactions respectives pour élargir l’impact de cette initiative. Lire aussi : Lutte contre la désinformation : L’Association EDEL en conférence internationale sur le sujet dans l’espace AES Nadège KINDA Minute.bf

items.title: Face à OpenAI, Google remanie en profondeur sa division IA
items.description: Google a annoncé une importante réorganisation de sa division d'intelligence artificielle DeepMind, dans un contexte de concurrence accrue avec OpenAI et Anthropic. Le groupe américain revoit la gouvernance de son laboratoire d'IA tout en faisant face au départ de plusieurs chercheurs de premier plan. Figure emblématique de DeepMind et lauréat du prix Nobel de chimie 2024, Demis Hassabis quitte ses fonctions de directeur général de la filiale. Il devient président de DeepMind et directeur scientifique d'Alphabet, la maison mère de Google, afin de se consacrer au développement de l'intelligence artificielle générale (AGI), qu'il estime désormais « à portée de main ». La direction opérationnelle de DeepMind est désormais confiée à Koray Kavukcuoglu, jusqu'ici directeur technique du laboratoire. Nommé vice-président senior, il sera directement rattaché au directeur général de Google et d'Alphabet, Sundar Pichai, un choix qui, selon plusieurs médias américains, traduit une volonté d'accélérer la commercialisation des technologies d'intelligence artificielle du groupe. Cette réorganisation intervient alors que Google cherche à combler son retard sur ses principaux concurrents. Malgré les progrès réalisés avec sa famille de modèles Gemini, le lancement de Gemini 3.5 Pro, attendu depuis plusieurs semaines, n'a toujours pas eu lieu, tandis qu'OpenAI et Anthropic ont déjà dévoilé de nouveaux modèles salués pour leurs performances, notamment en génération de code. En parallèle, Google doit également composer avec une vague de départs. Après 27 années passées au sein de l'entreprise, Jeff Dean, considéré comme l'un des architectes des infrastructures techniques de Google, quitte le groupe pour cofonder la start-up Discovery Loop avec les chercheurs Sanjay Ghemawat, Oriol Vinyals et Quoc Le. Cette nouvelle société ambitionne d'utiliser l'intelligence artificielle pour automatiser la recherche scientifique. Google restera toutefois associé à ce projet en investissant dans la jeune entreprise et en lui fournissant des capacités de calcul. Cette réorganisation s'inscrit dans un contexte de forte concurrence pour attirer et conserver les meilleurs talents de l'IA. Ces derniers mois, plusieurs chercheurs de renom ont quitté Google, notamment Noam Shazeer, parti rejoindre OpenAI, et John Jumper, co-lauréat du prix Nobel avec Demis Hassabis, qui a intégré Anthropic. Avec cette nouvelle organisation, Google espère renforcer sa compétitivité dans un secteur où la bataille pour le leadership technologique s'intensifie de mois en mois. The post Face à OpenAI, Google remanie en profondeur sa division IA appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Only 13% of Africans have heard of AfCFTA as support for free trade surges to 62% – Afrobarometer
items.description: A new Afrobarometer report has revealed a striking paradox in African public opinion: while support for free trade is growing across the continent, awareness of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) – the flagship agreement designed to boost intra-African commerce – remains remarkably low. The findings are contained in the 2026 African Insights flagship report titled “Beyond Borders: Citizen Perspectives on a Shifting Global Order,” which draws on nationally representative surveys conducted across 38 African countries in 2024/2025. According to the report, only 13% of Africans have heard of the AfCFTA, despite it being one of the most ambitious economic integration initiatives in history. Awareness ranges from highs of about one-quarter of respondents in Guinea-Bissau (27%), Gabon (26%), and Cabo Verde (24%) to mere handfuls in Tunisia (5%) and Mauritania (4%). Even in Ghana, one of the first countries to ratify the agreement and home to the AfCFTA Secretariat, only 17% of citizens are aware of it. At the same time, support for the principle of free trade has surged significantly. More than six in 10 Africans (62%) now agree that it is “better for our economy if the government makes it easier for [our country] to trade with other countries to create economic opportunities,” compared to just one in three (34%) who would limit trade to protect local producers. This represents a substantial shift from just five years ago when only a slim majority (51%) held this view. Support for free trade is a majority position in 32 of the 38 surveyed countries, with Central Africa (65%), West Africa (65%), and Southern Africa (64%) all exhibiting strong support collectively. Liberia (86%), Eswatini (85%), and Chad (79%) recorded the highest levels of support. However, the report also found that Africans prefer to trade globally rather than limit themselves to the continent or subregion. Two-thirds (66%) say their governments should expand trading relationships globally, compared to minorities who favour prioritising the continent (20%) or the subregion (8%). “Despite being one of the most ambitious economic-integration projects in history, the AfCFTA remains largely unknown to ordinary Africans,” the report states. “Awareness is heavily skewed toward the better-educated and regular news consumers, suggesting a disconnect between elite-level policy ambition and public reach.” The report warns that African governments should not assume popular support for the AfCFTA will follow automatically. “They will need to invest in targeted public education and domestic communication strategies that clearly explain how intra-African trade serves as a stepping stone to broader global economic competitiveness – or risk pursuing a landmark agreement without the public mandate needed to sustain it.” The 2026 African Insights report is the third in Afrobarometer’s annual flagship series, examining citizen attitudes on trade, migration, great-power competition, global voice, and climate change across the continent.

items.title: Rethinking talent acquisition in banking, finance and insurance
items.description: Ask almost any HR leader in Ghana’s banking, finance or insurance sector about hiring, and you’ll hear a familiar story. Hundreds of applications arrive for a single vacancy, sometimes thousands, yet building a strong shortlist remains surprisingly difficult. The challenge is not a shortage of applicants. It is the increasing complexity of identifying people who can succeed in an industry that is changing faster than ever. Institutions that build the strongest teams over the next five years are unlikely to be those that fill vacancies the fastest. They will be those that understand how their talent market has changed and adjust their hiring strategies accordingly. Part of that story begins with Ghana’s banking sector clean-up. Between 2017 and 2019, mergers, licence revocations and market exits reshaped the industry. Beyond reducing the number of institutions, the exercise changed the labour market. Some professionals left banking altogether, while others became more deliberate about where they chose to build their careers. That shift coincided with the rapid growth of digital financial services, creating new opportunities for professionals with banking experience and expanding the range of employers competing for the same skills. The Competition Has Moved Beyond Banking If the banking sector clean-up reshaped the market, the rapid growth of digital financial services has accelerated that change. According to the Bank of Ghana (2024), fintechs in Ghana processed more than GH¢514 billion in transactions in the first quarter of 2024 alone, while the country continues to rank among the world’s leading mobile money markets. Financial services are no longer delivered exclusively by banks. Telecommunications companies, fintechs and technology firms are now competing for the same customers and, increasingly, the same talent. The sales executive, compliance specialist, data analyst or digital product manager that a bank hopes to recruit may also be considering opportunities in fintech, telecommunications or technology companies. Experienced professionals have more options than they did a decade ago, and employers are recruiting in a much broader labour market. What We See From the Marketplace Recruitment data often tells a different story from application numbers. Across our work with employers in banking, finance and insurance, we regularly see vacancies attract substantial interest while producing relatively few candidates who meet the full requirements of the role. High application volume should not be mistaken for strong talent supply. The real constraint for many employers is the quality of the shortlist, not the size of the applicant pool. The pattern is particularly evident in specialist and leadership positions. In recent recruitment assignments, roles such as Chief Financial Officer, Compliance, Audit, Banking Operations, Digital Sales, Digital Innovation and Transformation, Business Development, Recovery and Relationship Management have consistently proved the most difficult to shortlist. The challenge is rarely a lack of applicants. Employers are looking for professionals who combine technical expertise with commercial judgement, industry knowledge and, increasingly, the ability to work across digital environments. Those combinations remain relatively scarce. We are also seeing sustained demand for capabilities in compliance, digital transformation, data and customer-facing commercial roles. Banks are not the only organisations looking for these skills. Fintechs, payment service providers and other businesses operating in financial services are recruiting from the same talent pool, increasing competition for experienced professionals. These observations provide employers with a perspective that vacancy reports alone cannot. They show where capability is becoming scarce, where hiring timelines are likely to extend and where organisations may need to rethink how they attract talent. Recruitment Is Increasingly a Business Decision Once competition extends beyond traditional rivals, recruitment becomes more than an HR function. It becomes a business decision. For years, banks invested heavily in developing professionals with expertise in customer relationship management, risk, compliance and digital banking. Those investments were expected to strengthen the institution over the long term. Today, many of those same capabilities are valuable well beyond banking. A relationship manager with years of experience serving corporate clients may be just as attractive to a fintech expanding its business banking offering. A compliance professional with deep regulatory expertise can move into payment services or digital finance. Professionals leading digital innovation are increasingly able to move between banks, fintechs and technology companies with relative ease. This changes how recruitment challenges should be interpreted. Hiring is no longer simply about replacing someone who has left. It is about understanding which capabilities are becoming harder to secure, who else is competing for them and how organisations can continue building the workforce they need. Viewed this way, recruitment is not simply an HR process. It is a business decision that directly influences an organisation’s ability to compete, innovate and grow. How Employers Can Respond Understanding the shift is the first step. Responding to it is where competitive advantage is built. One response is to broaden where talent comes from. If fintechs and technology companies recruit experienced bankers, banks can also recruit professionals whose expertise has been developed outside traditional financial institutions. Looking only at direct competitors narrows the available talent pool. Employers should also look beyond application numbers when assessing the health of their recruitment strategy. A role that attracts hundreds of applications but consistently produces weak shortlists may require a different sourcing strategy, stronger employer branding or earlier engagement with specialist talent. Finally, organisations should treat scarce capabilities as a pipeline challenge rather than a vacancy challenge. Compliance, digital transformation, data and specialist commercial roles are unlikely to become easier to recruit. Institutions that build graduate pathways, invest in internal development and maintain relationships with talent partners before vacancies arise will be better positioned than those that begin searching only after a resignation. Looking Beyond the Vacancy The strongest organisations over the next five years are unlikely to be those that recruit fastest. They will be those that understand how their talent market is changing and adjust before that change becomes a constraint. Looking beyond today’s vacancy means asking different questions. Which capabilities are becoming harder to secure? Which organisations are attracting the professionals we want to retain? How should our workforce evolve to support the business we expect to become? These are no longer questions for HR alone. They influence growth, resilience and the ability to compete in an industry where technology continues to reshape customer expectations. Talent has become one of the few advantages that competitors cannot easily replicate. Institutions that recognise this will do more than improve recruitment. They will strengthen their capacity to adapt in a financial services market that continues to evolve. Reference: Bank of Ghana. (2024). Summary of economic and financial data (Statistical Report). items.title: CDF Munir discusses enhancement of defence, security cooperation with Somalia: ISPR
items.description: Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir discussed the enhancement of bilateral defence and security cooperation with Somalia in a meeting with the country’s defence minister, the military’s media wing said on Thursday. According to a press release by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), a high-level defence delegation from Somalia called on the CDF at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi. The delegation was led by Somalia’s Defence Minister Ahmed Moallim Fiqi, the ISPR said. CDF Munir reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to “supporting Somalia in strengthening its security apparatus and fostering enduring peace in the region”, the statement added. During the meeting, “matters of mutual interest, regional security dynamics, and measures to further enhance bilateral defence and security cooperation were discussed”, it said, adding that both sides underscored the importance of “deepening military-to-military ties and capacity building initiatives to counter common security challenges”. The visiting dignitary appreciated Pakistan’s steadfast support and the professional role played by the Pakistan Armed Forces in promoting regional peace and stability, the ISPR said. The previous day, the naval and air force chiefs reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening defence ties with Somalia and supporting institutional cooperation with its air force in separate meetings with the Somali delegation, the military’s media wing said on Wednesday. At the meeting at Naval Headquarters with Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf, the leaders discussed “key matters of mutual professional interest, regional maritime security and bilateral defence collaboration”, according to the statement. The naval chief reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening defence ties with Somalia. Meanwhile, in a meeting with Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Baber Sidhu at Air Headquarters, discussions focused on bilateral defence cooperation, professional collaboration and capacity building, the statement said. The Somali defence minister lauded the Pakistan Navy’s contributions to regional maritime security, alongside PAF’s professionalism and operational capabilities. Pakis­tan and Somalia agreed in January to strengthen collaboration in training, border management, disaster management and the adoption of a joint strategy against terrorism to deepen cooperation in internal security. The agreement was reached as Pakistan’s Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met a high-level Somali delegation led by Somalia’s Interior Minister Ali Yusuf at the Ministry of Interior.

items.title: Davido-Uzodimma : Imo aide says comment was personal, not Governor’s position
items.description: The Senior Special Assistant to the Imo State Governor on Electronic and Creative Media, Ambrose Nwaogwugwu, has clarified that a statement circulating online regarding Afrobeats star, David Adeleke, popularly known as Davido, was his personal opinion and not that of Governor Hope Uzodimma. Nwaogwugwu, in a statement issued on Thursday, said the statement was authored by him in his capacity as a private citizen commenting on a topical national issue, and should not have been attributed to the Imo State governor. He said the attribution had created a wrong impression, urging media platforms and bloggers to correct what he described as a misrepresentation. “The comments being credited to the Governor by some bloggers are a clear misrepresentation of the facts. “It is unfortunate that some bloggers chose to attribute the statement to the Governor when it was, in fact, a personal opinion I expressed in my capacity as a private citizen commenting on a topical national issue,” Nwaogwugwu stated. He explained that official statements on behalf of Governor Uzodimma are issued by the Chief Press Secretary, while the Imo State Commissioner for Information speaks for the state government, except where other officials are expressly authorised. The clarification followed reports linking the governor to comments on Davido’s recent call for a free and fair governorship election in Osun State. Davido had, during a press conference on Wednesday, appealed to an unnamed politician from Imo State to allow the people of Osun to freely choose their preferred candidate in the August 15 governorship election. The singer, while alleging concerns over possible interference in the poll, urged political actors to promote peace and respect the will of voters. Reacting to the development, Nwaogwugwu said his response was made in his personal capacity and did not represent the position of Governor Uzodimma or the Imo State Government. He urged media practitioners to exercise caution in attributing comments to public officials, stressing the need for accuracy, fairness and responsible journalism. “It is therefore inappropriate to attribute a harmless personal opinion that I authored in my personal capacity to the Governor, particularly when the statement did not indicate that I was speaking on his behalf,” he added. Nwaogwugwu subsequently called on media platforms that published the report to make corrections in order to properly reflect the source and context of the statement.
