items.title: Only 13% of Africans aware of AfCFTA despite growing support for free trade — Afrobarometer
items.description: Although the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is regarded as one of the continent’s most ambitious economic integration initiatives, only 13 per cent of Africans have heard of the agreement, according to the latest Afrobarometer African Insights 2026 report. The report, titled ‘Beyond Borders: Citizen Perspectives on a Shifting Global Order,’ indicates that while public awareness of the landmark trade agreement remains strikingly low, support for freer trade between African countries and the rest of the world continues to grow. The study, which draws on Round 10 Afrobarometer survey data collected across 38 African countries between 2024 and 2025, explores how Africans perceive global trade, migration, international influence, climate change and geopolitical developments. According to the report, awareness of the AfCFTA is concentrated largely among highly educated and politically informed citizens, with no surveyed country recording awareness levels above 27 per cent. Despite this knowledge gap, the survey found that 62 per cent of Africans believe their countries would benefit economically by making trade easier with other nations. The figure represents a significant increase from 51 per cent recorded five years earlier, highlighting growing public confidence in international trade as a driver of economic growth. Support for freer trade emerged as the majority view in 32 of the 38 countries surveyed. Economic hardship One of the report’s most notable findings challenges conventional global assumptions about public attitudes towards trade. While economic hardship in many parts of the world often fuels protectionist sentiments, Afrobarometer found the opposite pattern across Africa. Rather than calling for greater economic isolation, many Africans continue to favour increased openness to regional and international markets despite difficult economic conditions. The report suggests this reflects widespread expectations that stronger trade relations could create jobs, stimulate investment and improve living standards across the continent. Immigration attitudes The survey also uncovered an unexpected trend regarding immigration. Contrary to patterns observed in many other regions of the world, resistance to immigration in Africa is strongest among wealthier, better-educated and more highly skilled citizens, as well as residents of the continent’s more prosperous countries. According to the report, these groups may perceive immigrants as competitors for relatively scarce formal employment opportunities, even though they are generally better positioned economically than the wider population. Outward-looking continent Overall, Afrobarometer describes Africa as a continent that remains outward-looking and increasingly engaged with global opportunities, while also becoming more strategic in how its citizens assess international relationships. The report notes that Africa’s future will depend significantly on how governments navigate complex global challenges, including international trade, geopolitical competition, migration and climate change. It further emphasises that while citizens generally support deeper engagement with the global economy, greater public education will be needed to ensure Africans fully understand continental initiatives such as the AfCFTA, which is intended to boost intra-African trade, industrialisation and long-term economic integration.

items.title: Okoe Boye accuses Mahama government of prioritising arrests over jobs for youth
items.description: Former Health Minister Dr Bernard Okoe Boye has criticised the Mahama administration over what he describes as increasing arrests of young people over their social media activity. He argued that the government’s actions are at odds with the promises it made before the 2024 elections. Speaking during the NPP’s Democracy Under Attack demonstration on Thursday, August 6, Dr Okoe Boye said the government’s approach contradicts the expectations of Ghanaians and warned that it risks creating a perception that the administration is prioritising arrests over employment. “This is not what you promised the people of Ghana. In fact, it is possible that by the end of this year, this government would have arrested more youth than it has created jobs for the youth,” he stated. He said while public discourse should be responsible, alleged offenders should be dealt with through the courts rather than through arrests. “What we are saying is that people should engage in responsible speech. If it is irresponsible, take them to court,” he said. He questioned whether the National Democratic Congress (NDC) would have won the 2024 general election if it had campaigned on a promise to arrest people for their social media posts. “If John Mahama and the NDC had told Ghanaians that when we come there will be discipline and nobody should post anything on TikTok or we will arrest you, do you think they would have come to power?” he asked.

items.title: Free El-Rufai too, Atiku challenges Tinubu over EFCC’s Osun climbdown
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to direct the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission ICPC to release former Kaduna State Governor, Nasir El-Rufai, arguing that if the president could order the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission EFCC to vacate its freeze on Osun State’s government account, he has no basis to claim powerlessness over El-Rufai’s continued detention. The African Democratic Congress ADC presidential candidate said on Thursday in a statement by his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communication, Phrank Shaibu, that Tinubu’s intervention in the Osun matter had demolished the long-held claim that anti-corruption agencies act independently of the Presidency. “Having now demonstrated that he can issue direct operational directives to anti-corruption agencies whenever he considers it expedient, President Tinubu owes Nigerians an explanation as to why he cannot exercise the same authority in the case of Mallam Nasir El-Rufai. “If he can direct the EFCC to discontinue its action today, then he cannot pretend to be powerless over the actions of the ICPC tomorrow”, Atiku declared. He faulted what he described as conflicting accounts from the government over the Osun freeze. “If indeed there was a court order, why did the EFCC omit such a fundamental fact from its official account? If there was none, then the President has introduced into the public discourse a legal process that exists nowhere in the EFCC’s own narrative. Nigerians deserve a coherent explanation instead of conflicting versions from the same government,” he said. He argued that the President could not simultaneously deny interference in EFCC operations while directing the commission’s next move. “Institutions cannot be independent only when it is politically convenient and subject to presidential directives whenever controversy arises. That is not institutional autonomy; it is executive control disguised as independence.” According to Atiku, the implications extend beyond the fate of one state or one detained politician, going to the heart of public trust in Nigeria’s anti-graft architecture. He added that reversing the Osun freeze, coming just days before the state’s governorship election, does not resolve the deeper questions the episode has raised. “Democracy is not measured by the ability to reverse an injustice after public outrage; it is measured by the discipline to prevent such injustice from occurring in the first place”, he stated. items.title: Simandou : Rio Tinto SimFer confirme sa montée en puissance vers un objectif de 60 millions de tonnes par an
items.description: Les responsables de Rio Tinto SimFer ont affiché leur confiance dans l'évolution du projet Simandou lors d'une conférence de presse organisée ce jeudi à Conakry. Face aux journalistes, le directeur général de SimFer S.A., Chris Aitchison, le directeur pays de Rio Tinto, Aboubacar Koulibaly et le nouveau directeur des opérations, ont présenté les progrès enregistrés sur les volets minier, ferroviaire et portuaire, tout en mettant en avant les retombées économiques, sociales et humaines attendues pour la Guinée. Selon le directeur général de SimFer S.A, Chris Aitchison, le projet poursuit sa transition entre la phase de construction et celle de l'exploitation, avec des infrastructures qui avancent conformément au calendrier établi. « Les travaux de construction de la mine SimFer et des infrastructures portuaires ont désormais dépassé les trois quarts de leur réalisation, tandis que la mise en service complète des infrastructures ferroviaires a été achevée au premier trimestre », a-t-il déclaré. Il a également présenté les performances opérationnelles enregistrées au cours du premier semestre 2026. L'entreprise a expédié 2,2 millions de tonnes de minerai de fer, dont 1,6 million de tonnes au seul deuxième trimestre, principalement vers la Chine. Les premières livraisons affichent une teneur moyenne en fer de 65,8 %, confirmant, selon lui, « la qualité exceptionnelle du minerai de Simandou ». Sur le plan de la production, SimFer indique avoir produit 1,2 million de tonnes de minerai durant le premier semestre, dont 700 000 tonnes au deuxième trimestre, grâce à la montée en puissance progressive des opérations. Chris Aitchison a précisé que la construction de la mine est réalisée à environ 77 %, tandis que les infrastructures portuaires affichent un taux d'exécution de 85 %. La mise en service du concasseur primaire est attendue au quatrième trimestre 2026, alors que celle du port de SimFer demeure prévue au premier trimestre 2027. À terme, le projet vise une capacité annuelle de 60 millions de tonnes de minerai de fer, avec une pleine production annoncée pour le second semestre 2028. Au-delà des performances industrielles, les responsables de SimFer ont insisté sur les retombées sociales du projet. Au cours du trimestre écoulé, l'entreprise a notamment inauguré un Centre d'inclusion numérique à Beyla, accompagné l'aménagement de 40 hectares de périmètres maraîchers dans 25 villages, formé 360 jeunes diplômés au développement de projets et recruté une deuxième cohorte d'apprentis composée à 50 % de femmes. Les effectifs mobilisés sur les activités minières, ferroviaires et portuaires atteignent désormais 19 460 travailleurs, avec un taux de participation guinéenne de 76 %. « Ces résultats illustrent notre engagement en faveur de l’emploi local, du renforcement des compétences nationales et du développement du capital humain guinéen », a affirmé Chris Aitchison. Il a par ailleurs présenté le nouveau directeur des opérations, Gomba, arrivé en mai 2026. Fort de plus de vingt années d'expérience dans l'industrie minière, notamment au sein de Rio Tinto en Afrique du Sud, il aura pour mission de piloter la préparation opérationnelle et la montée en puissance des activités minières de Simandou. De son côté, le directeur pays de Rio Tinto, Aboubacar Koulibaly, a mis l'accent sur l'impact structurant que représente Simandou pour l'économie guinéenne. « Cela va être une opportunité unique pour transformer le pays en termes de ressources publiques qui seront générées par les deux mines », a-t-il souligné, rappelant que les projets de SimFer et de Winning consortium constitueront d'importantes sources de revenus pour l'État. Il a également insisté sur les opportunités offertes aux entreprises nationales grâce aux exigences du contenu local. « Ce sont plusieurs milliards de dollars qui seront investis dans des entreprises guinéennes. Cela permettra à ces entreprises d’employer davantage de Guinéens et de créer plus de richesses », a-t-il indiqué. Mais pour le responsable de Rio Tinto, l'héritage le plus important du projet reste le développement du capital humain. « Notre objectif est de voir demain des Guinéens devenir des dirigeants comme Chris ou Kox, gérer Simandou puis exporter leur expertise à l'international. C'est cela le véritable héritage », a-t-il déclaré. Il a enfin mis en avant les standards internationaux de gouvernance, de transparence, d'intégrité et de performance environnementale appliqués par Rio Tinto, estimant qu'ils constitueront un héritage durable pour le secteur privé guinéen. « Nous voulons laisser à la Guinée des entreprises capables d'être compétitives sur le plan international, grâce aux meilleures pratiques en matière de gouvernance, de transparence et d'intégrité », a-t-il conclu. items.title: Gombe Police declare zero tolerance for traffic offenders, begin enforcement drive
items.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Gombe State Police Command has declared a zero-tolerance policy against traffic violations as it intensifies enforcement of road safety laws across the state. The Command said the move followed the directive of the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, aimed at restoring order on the roads and reducing avoidable accidents. In a statement issued on Thursday by the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Buhari Abdullahi, on behalf of the Commissioner of Police, the Command expressed concern over increasing disregard for traffic regulations, saying the development had contributed to congestion, obstruction of vehicular movement, road crashes and loss of lives and property. The Command warned that all traffic offenders, including serving security personnel, would face sanctions in accordance with existing laws. It added that vehicles found violating traffic regulations would be impounded, while offenders could be prosecuted where necessary. The statement further directed all officers and personnel of the Command to maintain the highest level of discipline and professionalism during enforcement operations, stressing that no police officer was exempt from obeying road safety rules. The Commissioner of Police, CP Umar Ahmed Chuso, urged motorists, commercial drivers, tricycle and motorcycle operators, as well as other road users, to comply with traffic regulations, obey road signs, avoid reckless driving and cooperate with law enforcement agencies. Chuso said strict adherence to traffic laws remained essential to protecting lives, safeguarding property and ensuring smooth movement of vehicles across the state. He reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to enhancing public safety, maintaining order on the roads and promoting responsible road use among residents of Gombe State. items.title: 2027: NDC leaders clash over Gombe structure as campaigns approach
items.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe Less than two weeks before the commencement of campaigns for the 2027 general elections, disagreement has emerged among leaders of the National Democratic Coalition (NDC) in Gombe State over the strength and preparedness of the party’s grassroots structure. The disagreement involving the Northeast Zonal Coordinator of the Coalition Alliance Network for the Peter Obi/Kwankwaso Movement, Alhaji Yahaya Mohammed Samaila; the party’s governorship hopeful in Gombe State, Dr. Babayo Ardo; and the National President of the Coalition Alliance Network, Mallam Zakari Garba Bura, has sparked debate over the party’s readiness for the upcoming elections. While Samaila alleged that the NDC lacks a visible and effective political structure in the state, Ardo and Bura disagreed, insisting that the party has established functional structures across Gombe’s 11 local government areas. Speaking in Gombe, Samaila described the party’s presence in the state as weak compared with other states in the Northeast, citing the absence of campaign materials and visible organisational activities. “We don’t have structures compared to other states in the Northeast. We don’t have a single vehicle branded with the NDC logo in Gombe for campaigns. There are no posters of governorship, House of Assembly or senatorial candidates across the state,” he said. Although he described Ardo as “a very good man,” Samaila expressed concern over what he considered limited visibility and accessibility of the governorship hopeful among party supporters. He said efforts were ongoing to mobilise support groups and associations to strengthen the party’s grassroots presence ahead of the campaign season. “If we receive support from other groups and associations, within two weeks we can build a formidable structure in Gombe State. But it requires funding and sponsorship,” he said. Samaila also disclosed that he was unaware of any campaign committee for Ardo and had not seen evidence of a fully organised campaign team. However, reacting during an online interview from Abuja, Bura dismissed the concerns, insisting that the coalition has a strong nationwide network. According to him, the coalition has representatives across Nigeria’s 774 local government areas and more than 8,000 political wards. “We have representatives in all the wards, and our plan is to deploy 10 members to every polling unit. We have between 200,000 and 400,000 members in our support groups,” he said. Speaking specifically on Gombe State, Bura said the coalition had established structures across all 11 local government areas and 114 wards. “Go to Hinna, Akko, Dukku and Nafada, and you will see our network of elders, women and youths. We have a strong structure in Gombe,” he stated. He, however, clarified that the coalition had not officially announced its governorship candidate, while expressing optimism that Ardo would emerge as the party’s flag bearer. Bura said the coalition plans to build on the support recorded by Peter Obi and Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso in the Northeast during the last general election. Also reacting, Ardo dismissed claims that the NDC lacks grassroots support, describing the party as a young but fast-growing political platform. “NDC is only about six months old, having been registered in February 2026, but within that short period we have made tremendous progress,” he said. “In Gombe State, we have established unit committees, ward executives, local government executives and a state executive. Anybody who says NDC has no structure is simply mistaken.” The governorship hopeful said the party would embark on a statewide tour of the 11 local government areas to engage residents and prepare for campaigns in line with the timetable of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). He said his administration, if elected, would prioritise security through community participation and stronger collaboration with security agencies, economic development driven by agriculture, commerce and investment, improved education standards and enhanced healthcare delivery. Ardo stressed that his campaign would focus on issues rather than personalities. “Our campaign will be issue-based. We want to discuss where Gombe should be in the next 10 to 50 years, not engage in personal attacks,” he said. Addressing the disagreement among party stakeholders, Ardo called for unity and collaboration. “I don’t know the zonal coordinator personally, but I can assure him that NDC is solid in Gombe State. We should work together, focus on issues and build synergy instead of exchanging personal attacks,” he added. items.title: Crise à l’EDG : les prestataires maintiennent la pression après une première rencontre sans « entente »
items.description: Après leur mobilisation de protestation de mardi dernier, les prestataires d’Électricité de Guinée (EDG) maintiennent la pression. Ils réclament notamment leur embauche ainsi qu’une amélioration de leurs conditions de vie et de travail après plusieurs années de services. Au lendemain de cette mobilisation, les représentants des protestataires ont été reçus mercredi par la Direction générale d’EDG, au siège de la société, à la Minière. Cette rencontre, tenue à huis clos et prolongée jusqu’à tard dans la soirée, avait pour objectif d’ouvrir des discussions afin de trouver une issue à la crise. Mais, à l’issue de cette première rencontre, aucun accord n’a été trouvé entre les deux parties. Interrogé ce jeudi 6 août 2026 par Guineenews, Daouda Condé, porte-parole de circonstance des protestataires, a livré les détails des échanges avec la Direction générale. Aucun accord à l’issue de la rencontre Selon Daouda Condé, un des représentants des prestataires qui étaient au tour de la table, les discussions n’ont pas permis de rapprocher les positions. Il assure que la mobilisation se poursuivra tant qu’une réponse concrète ne sera pas apportée à leurs revendications. « Il n'y a pas d'entente d'abord entre la Direction et nous donc, la mobilisation continue. La Direction nous a reçus pour écouter nos préoccupations. Ce qu'ils nous on dit hier n'était pas clair, ça ne nous convenait pas. On ne sait pas si nos revendications vont êtres prises en charge mais pour le moment, la mobilisation continue » , nous a-t-il confié. Cette déclaration traduit la persistance du désaccord entre les prestataires et leur Direction, alors que leurs revendications portent principalement sur leur situation professionnelle et leurs conditions de travail. Une nouvelle rencontre annoncée mardi prochain Malgré l’absence d’accord lors de cette première séance de discussions, le dialogue devrait se poursuivre. Une nouvelle rencontre est annoncée pour mardi prochain, au cours de laquelle la Direction générale devrait communiquer sa position sur les revendications formulées par les prestataires. « La Direction nous a convoqués le mardi à venir pour donner une réponse à nos revendications » , a-t-il annoncé. En attendant cette échéance, les prestataires disent maintenir leur mobilisation, dans l’attente d’une réponse susceptible de permettre une sortie de crise.

items.title: Security forces kill 12 terrorists in Balochistan's Mastung, Washuk IBOs: ISPR
items.description: Security forces conducted two intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan’s Washuk and Mastung districts, killing 12 terrorists in total, the military’s media wing said on Thursday. In a statement, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said the “high-tempo” operations were carried out as part of the ‘Radul Fitna’ counterterrorism campaign against Fitna-al-Hindustan in Balochistan. Balochistan-based terrorist groups have been designated as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan. The ISPR said that on August 5, “[The] movement of six terrorists was picked up by the security forces in Washuk District of Balochistan. Own troops effectively engaged these terrorists. As a result of precise and skilful engagement, all six terrorists belonging to Indian proxy, Fitna-al-Hindustan were sent to hell.” The military’s media wing further said that during an operation in the Mastung district earlier today, six terrorists were “sent to hell after the intense fire exchange between armed forces and the terrorists”, while a terrorist hideout was also destroyed. “Under vision ‘Azm-i-Istehkam’ (as approved by [the] Federal Apex Committee on National Action Plan), security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan will continue at full pace to wipe out [the] menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country,” the statement concludes. Last Wednesday, eight terrorists belonging to Fitna-al-Hindustan were killed after an “ intense engagement ” in Balochistan’s Nushki district during multiple intelligence-based operations, the ISPR said. “Weapons, ammunition and improvised explosive devices used by terrorists were also recovered and destroyed during the operations,” it added. In July, security forces and law enforcement personnel jointly launched Operation Shaban in Balochistan in retaliation for a deadly attack on a police post at the Mangi Dam pumping station in Ziarat on July 6. During that assault, armed attackers kidnapped and killed 27 police officers . Later, security forces also launched Operation Al-Azm in the province after a shooting on a Karachi-bound coach coming from Quetta claimed three lives and injured five others last week. A monthly security assessment released in early June by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS) said that after two consecutive months of improvement, Pakistan’s security situation deteriorated sharply in May, driven primarily by escalating terrorist violence in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan. The report said Balochistan emerged as the most affected province during the month. The province recorded 71 terrorist attacks, compared with 34 in April, representing a 109pc increase. The deteriorating security situation was further reflected in a surge in kidnappings, it said. Of the 54 abductions reported nationwide during May, 52 occurred in Balochistan alone, highlighting the growing operational reach and confidence of terrorist groups in the province, it said.

items.title: KMA denies claims of financial interest in Baba Yara Stadium prefabricated containers
items.description: The Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly has to clarify the scope of its post-demolition rebuilding plan at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium. The authorities say the re-emergence of the structures forms part of a planned redevelopment initiative aimed at creating a more organised and orderly trading environment. The clarification by Kumasi Mayor, Richard Kwasi Ofori Boadi Agyemang, comes amid growing confusion and allegations on social media that the Mayor has a personal financial interest in the prefabricated containers being installed around the facility. Addressing a special meeting of the Assembly at the Prempeh Assembly Hall, the Mayor described the claims as “false and malicious.” “Let me state clearly that I have no involvement in the sale, production, or supply of these containers. These allegations are false and they have caused me pain. I will not do anything to jeopardize the trust the people have in me,” he said. On July 31, a joint security taskforce led by the KMA demolished unauthorized structures around the Baba Yara Sports Stadium. At the time, authorities said the exercise was part of broader efforts to restore order, decongest the area, and improve sanitation around the national sports facility. However, barely four days after the demolition, construction workers were sighted laying foundations for new stalls in sections that had just been cleared. The rapid return of structures triggered questions from the public and traders about the motive behind the exercise. Some of the affected traders who have since re-erected their containers said the new design aligns with directives issued by the Mayor prior to the demolition. They commended the Assembly for allowing them to return under a more organized arrangement. So far, 14 traders have complied and re-erected their containers using the approved design. But not all traders are satisfied. Some food vendors have raised concerns about the new structures, citing potential fire and security risks. Dissatisfied traders are alleging that the Mayor is benefiting financially from the prefabricated containers. Others have also accused him of overpricing the structures and claimed the containers do not meet the standards he set. Meanwhile, the Kumasi Mayor revealed that it was the traders who approached him with their own contractor, appealing to be allowed to set up the new prefabricated containers. “The KMA has not benefited from the new structures. The traders themselves were asked to put up these standard structures in compliance with our standard design that will give a beautiful facelift to the stadium area and Kumasi at large. It was the traders who hired their own contractor to work on the project. I was not involved in the process or the payment arrangements,” he stated. He also dismissed claims and speculations that the Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly’s (KMA) decision to remove traders and occupants is aimed at replacing them with new occupants affiliated with the government and the ruling party. He expressed concern over why he is being accused amid the development. Mr Boadi said that he only intervened to facilitate discussions with the contractor after concerns were raised about the initial cost, leading to a bulk discount for traders. He explained that the contract for the project was not awarded by the KMA. In the interest of transparency, accountability, and to avoid any conflict of interest, the Mayor stressed that the Assembly will not accommodate any additional traders beyond the 14 who were affected and who have complied with the directive. “If they are accusing me of something I know nothing about, then let me be clear: only the 14 traders who have complied with the Assembly’s directive to acquire the approved prefabricated stores will be permitted to return to the designated area. No additional trader will be allowed to occupy the area, regardless of whether they are ready to follow the directive or not,” he said.

items.title: Casablanca : TGCC décroche le marché de reconstruction du stade Tessema pour 1,8 milliard de dirhams
items.description: L'entreprise marocaine TGCC a remporté le marché de reconstruction du stade Tessema, à Casablanca, pour un montant d'environ 1,824 milliard de dirhams. Cette nouvelle étape marque le lancement de la phase principale de ce projet de modernisation d'une infrastructure sportive emblématique de la métropole. Attribué à l'issue d'un appel d'offres, le marché a opposé uniquement TGCC à SGTM, les deux seules entreprises ayant présenté une offre. Avec une proposition de 1,824 milliard de dirhams, TGCC s'est imposée devant SGTM, dont l'offre s'élevait à 1,883 milliard de dirhams. Ce contrat constitue la deuxième phase du projet, après l'achèvement du premier lot consacré aux travaux de démolition, de terrassement et de nivellement. Celui-ci avait été confié il y a près de deux mois à l'entreprise SNTRO, pour un montant de 36,4 millions de dirhams. La nouvelle phase comprend l'ensemble des travaux de construction et d'équipement du futur stade. Elle englobe notamment les gros œuvres, la réalisation de la structure en béton, les travaux d'étanchéité, les structures métalliques et la couverture, ainsi que les revêtements extérieurs et intérieurs, les faux plafonds, les menuiseries, les travaux de peinture et les finitions. Le futur stade sera édifié sur un terrain de 6,62 hectares, situé dans l'arrondissement de Ben M'Sik-Sidi Othmane, à Casablanca. L'ancienne enceinte, devenue vétuste et ne répondant plus aux normes actuelles, a été entièrement démolie afin de laisser place à un complexe moderne. Le nouveau stade disposera d'une capacité de 30 000 places, avec une couverture partielle, et sera conçu pour accueillir diverses compétitions sportives dans des conditions conformes aux standards contemporains. Le projet avait déjà franchi plusieurs étapes importantes. En février dernier, le Laboratoire public d'essais et d'études (LPEE) s'était vu attribuer le marché des études géotechniques et du contrôle de qualité des travaux pour près de 7 millions de dirhams. En décembre 2025, le concours architectural avait permis de sélectionner le cabinet chargé de concevoir le futur stade, à l'issue d'une compétition ayant réuni onze équipes d'architectes. La reconstruction du stade Tessema s'inscrit dans le vaste programme de modernisation des infrastructures sportives marocaines, engagé en prévision des grandes compétitions internationales que le Royaume accueillera dans les prochaines années, notamment la Coupe d'Afrique des nations 2027 et la Coupe du monde 2030. items.title: Le Premier ministre Zeine s’engage pour la valorisation des filières du Kawar après la visite de l’APIK Baana…
items.description: Le Premier ministre, Ali Mahamane Lamine Zeine, a reçu, le mercredi 5 août 2026, une délégation de l’Association pour la Promotion de l’Intercommunalité au Kawar (APIK Baana), en présence du ministre de l’Agriculture et de l’Élevage, le Colonel Mahaman Elhadj Ousman. La rencontre a permis d’échanger autour des recommandations issues de la 2ᵉ édition de la Semaine du Kawar, une initiative dédiée à la promotion et au développement de cette région stratégique. Les membres de la délégation ont présenté au premier ministre, les préoccupations et propositions formulées lors de la Semaine du Kawar, en insistant particulièrement sur le développement des filières du sel, de la datte et du natron. Ces secteurs, fortement ancrés dans l’économie locale, ont été identifiés comme des leviers importants pour la création d’emplois, l’accroissement des revenus et la promotion d’une économie régionale résiliente. Le Premier ministre Zeine a écouté avec attention les doléances et recommandations soumises par l’APIK Baana. Il a indiqué avoir pris bonne note des propositions et réaffirmé l’engagement du Gouvernement à poursuivre les efforts nécessaires pour que les projets lancés répondent aux réalités et aux besoins des populations du Kawar. Il a souligné que le développement équilibré de toutes les régions du Niger demeure une priorité du président de la République, chef de l’état, le général d’armée Abdourahame tiani et elle est inscrite dans une dynamique de valorisation des potentialités locales au service d’une croissance durable et inclusive. Le ministre de l’Agriculture et de l’Élevage, le Colonel Mahaman Elhadj Ousman, a rappelé l’importance d’un accompagnement technique et financier ciblé pour structurer les filières concernées, améliorer les chaînes de valeur et faciliter l’accès aux marchés nationaux et internationaux. Les participants ont également évoqué la nécessité de renforcer les infrastructures locales, de soutenir la formation des acteurs et d’encourager les investissements privés respectueux des ressources naturelles. Les échanges se sont conclus sur la promesse d’un suivi concerté des recommandations, avec la mise en place de mécanismes de coordination entre l’État, les collectivités locales et les acteurs de la société civile. L’objectif affiché est d’assurer une mise en œuvre efficace des projets afin d’optimiser les retombées économiques et sociales pour les populations du Kawar. items.title: Aviation Funding: NAMA seeks 56% share of statutory charges
items.description: …AAAU demands 10% allocation for aviation manpower development By Gift ChapiOdekina,Abuja The Nigerian Airspace Management Agency (NAMA) has asked the National Assembly to increase its share of the statutory five per cent aviation revenue pool from the current 22 per cent to 56 per cent, warning that the rising cost of maintaining safety-critical infrastructure is putting increasing pressure on the country’s air navigation system. Managing Director of NAMA, Engr. Farouk Ahmed Umar, made the demand on Thursday at a public hearing organised by the House of Representatives Committee on Aviation, saying the existing revenue-sharing formula no longer reflects the scale of the agency’s statutory responsibilities or the financial burden of keeping Nigeria’s airspace safe. At the same hearing, the African Aviation and Aerospace University (AAAU), Abuja, asked the National Assembly to include it as a statutory beneficiary of the five per cent Ticket Sales Charge (TSC) and allocate not less than 10 per cent of the revenue to the institution for aviation manpower development, research and innovation. Umar told the lawmakers that the safety of the aviation sector depends on strong and adequately funded institutions, stressing that the regulator must be strong, meteorological services dependable, accident and incident investigation independent and aviation training excellent. He, however, said it was equally important for the law regulating the sector to recognise, in practical and sustainable terms, the enormous responsibility placed on NAMA as Nigeria’s sole Air Navigation Service Provider. According to him, NAMA currently receives only 22 per cent of the five per cent statutory revenue pool despite carrying a substantial portion of the operational responsibilities required for safe flight operations across the country. He therefore asked the National Assembly to increase NAMA’s allocation to 56 per cent of the available pool, stressing that the proposal would not increase the existing five per cent charge but would ensure a more sustainable allocation of the available revenue to the agency responsible for critical air navigation infrastructure. Umar said NAMA’s responsibilities begin long before passengers board an aircraft and continue throughout every stage of flight operations. “Long before a passenger boards an aircraft, NAMA’s personnel and systems are already at work. A flight plan must be processed, aeronautical information must be current. Radios must be clear. Navigation aids must be serviceable. Surveillance must be available. Controllers must be at their positions. Engineers must be ready to respond. Power and backup power must hold. “When the aircraft takes off, all these elements must come together, not later that day, not after a supplementary release, but at that very moment. “That is the nature of air navigation services. They are continuous, technology-intensive and unforgiving of delay. A broken office printer can wait until morning. A degraded safety-critical communication link cannot. A postponed meeting may be inconvenient. Deferred radar support, navigation-aid calibration or controller training can reduce the resilience of the national system,” he said. The NAMA boss told the Committee that the cost of keeping Nigerian airspace safe had outgrown the existing funding formula, pointing out that the agency recorded a total cost profile exceeding ₦43 billion in 2023. According to him, the expenditure included approximately ₦21 billion in personnel costs, more than ₦12 billion in capital expenditure and over ₦10 billion in overheads. “These are not abstract numbers. Behind them are controllers, engineers, communication systems, navigation aids, surveillance platforms, power systems, spares, software, calibration, training and facilities spread across our country. “At the same time, a navigation charge as low as ₦11,000 per flight had remained unchanged since June 2008. “Consider what has happened to the cost of fuel, electricity, foreign exchange, imported components, software licences and specialist training since 2008. The service has had to absorb today’s costs with yesterday’s tariff base. “The dedication of our workforce has helped bridge that gap, but dedication is not a substitute for a sustainable funding system,” Umar said. He also raised concerns over the Total Radar Coverage of Nigeria (TRACON) system, saying the ageing surveillance infrastructure now requires a deliberate renewal and transition programme. According to him, as equipment ages, spare parts become increasingly difficult to obtain while manufacturers’ support changes, making sustained investment in replacement and modernisation imperative. Umar said the global aviation system was also becoming increasingly digital, interconnected and exposed to cyber risks, requiring greater investment in performance-based navigation, digital aeronautical information, satellite-enabled surveillance and integrated flight-data systems. He said such technologies promised improved capacity and efficiency but required substantial investment in equipment, data quality, specialised skills and cybersecurity. The NAMA managing director also asked the National Assembly to recognise obstacle assessment and WGS-84 aeronautical surveys as chargeable technical services performed by the agency. He said NAMA was the only federal aviation agency that connected WGS-84 survey data, obstacle analysis, aeronautical information, procedure design and operational management of airspace within one technical chain. Umar maintained that while the regulatory component of Aviation Height Clearance should remain with the appropriate regulator, NAMA should be directly paid for technical services involving WGS-84 survey validation, obstacle assessment, procedure-impact analysis and field work. He further argued that adequately funding NAMA would produce benefits extending beyond the agency to airlines, airports, passengers, trade, tourism and national security. “An aircraft that moves safely and efficiently through Nigerian airspace is an economic activity enabled by invisible infrastructure. NAMA is not asking the National Assembly for a blank cheque. NAMA supports accountability equal to the responsibility we seek,” he said. Umar pledged NAMA’s support for automated collection and remittance of revenues, quarterly disclosure of receipts and projects, annual independent audits, transparent procurement and measurable performance indicators. “We are prepared to report what was received, what it purchased, which milestone was achieved and what improvement the user obtained,” he said. The NAMA boss also urged the National Assembly to harmonise existing aviation laws, pointing out that while the Civil Aviation Act currently provides a 22 per cent allocation to NAMA, the NAMA Act refers to 23 per cent in its Fund provisions. “The law should speak with one voice. The beneficiaries should be named correctly; the percentages should total 100 per cent; collection and remittance responsibilities should be unambiguous; and the effective date should be clear,” he said. Umar acknowledged that reallocating the statutory revenue pool would raise legitimate concerns among other aviation agencies, but argued that the final formula should be determined by audited costs, statutory mandates and risks rather than preserving historical percentages. “A regulator and an Air Navigation Service Provider are both indispensable, but their cost structures are not identical. The law should recognise those differences while ensuring that every safety institution remains viable,” he said. Making his final appeal, Umar asked the lawmakers to appreciate the critical infrastructure and personnel behind the management of Nigeria’s airspace. “When a pilot calls an air traffic controller over Nigerian airspace, that voice is more than a radio transmission. It is the sound of a national safety system working. “Behind it are years of training, towers and centres, antennas and links, radar and navigation aids, engineers and procedures, generators and batteries, software and vigilance. The country expects that voice to be clear, confident and continuously available. “I respectfully pray the National Assembly to approve a 56 per cent allocation to NAMA from the existing five per cent pool; harmonise the affected enactments; recognise obstacle assessment and WGS-84 aeronautical survey as chargeable NAMA technical services; establish transparent, automated remittance; and pair the enhanced allocation with firm accountability and oversight. “Give us the means and hold us to the result. Give Nigerian airspace the resilience it requires and require us to demonstrate that resilience. In doing so, this National Assembly will not simply amend a percentage. It will strengthen the safety, efficiency, sovereignty and future competitiveness of our nation’s airspace,” Umar said. Meanwhile, the African Aviation and Aerospace University, Abuja, asked the National Assembly to recognise aviation manpower development as a critical component of the industry deserving statutory funding. Presenting the university’s position paper, the Acting Vice-Chancellor, Mustapha Abdullahi said that AAAU occupies a unique position in Nigeria’s aviation ecosystem as the country’s specialised federal university dedicated to aviation, aerospace and allied disciplines. The institution said it was established specifically to develop the highly skilled manpower required to sustain Nigeria’s aviation industry and should therefore be recognised as a statutory beneficiary of the five per cent Ticket Sales Charge. According to the university, the proposed amendments to the aviation laws provide an opportunity to ensure that funding within the sector is aligned not only with immediate operational responsibilities but also with the long-term sustainability of aviation manpower development. AAAU argued that aviation safety ultimately depends on competent professionals, including air traffic managers, aeronautical engineers, aviation managers, safety specialists, meteorologists, airspace planners, aerospace scientists, airport managers and environmental specialists. items.title: PFIPC Probe: Family raises alarm over planned Reps’ interrogation of Adeyemi in custody
items.description: The family of Adeniyi Adeyemi, the purported Director-General of the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council (PFIPC), has raised concerns over an alleged attempt by members of the House of Representatives Ad-hoc Committee investigating the council to question him while in police custody without the presence of his lawyers. Adeyemi’s brother, Peter Adeyemi, who spoke with Punch on Thursday, alleged that members of the committee visited the facility where Adeyemi is being detained and sought to interrogate him, but that he declined to respond to questions in the absence of his legal representatives. According to him, the family was worried about the development and appealed to the committee to allow Adeyemi to respond to the allegations against him in the same public manner in which the accusations were made. “The Reps committee came and wanted to interrogate him, but he refused. They are still there trying to make him talk without any of his lawyers being present. We are crying out loud so that the right thing would be done. “He has stated that he wants to be quizzed the same way others who have accused him have spoken. It’s not that he is not willing to state his side of the story,” Peter said. The latest allegation by the family came a day after Adeyemi, through his lawyer, Ademola Oyedokun, objected to the committee’s plan to question him at an undisclosed location while he remains in police custody. In a statement issued on Wednesday, Oyedokun said his client welcomed the House investigation into the alleged establishment and operations of the PFIPC but opposed any form of private or closed-door interrogation. The lawyer argued that since allegations against Adeyemi were made publicly, he should also be allowed to respond publicly. “We have read that the committee intends to interview our client at an undisclosed date and place. We ask it, respectfully, to think again. Everyone else in this matter has been heard in public, and what has been said about our client was said in public. He should be allowed to answer in the same place it was said,” the statement read. The House committee had on Tuesday announced plans to question Adeyemi at an undisclosed location while he remains in police custody. Chairman of the committee, Yusuf Gagdi, explained that the arrangement was to avoid interfering with ongoing investigations being conducted by security agencies, including the Nigeria Police Force, Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) and Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC). Gagdi said the committee had invited Adeyemi but was informed by the police that he remained in custody based on an existing court order. He stressed that the National Assembly would not take any action capable of undermining the judiciary or violating the principle of separation of powers, noting that lawmakers lacked the authority to override a subsisting court order. The committee is investigating allegations surrounding the creation and activities of the PFIPC, including claims bordering on impersonation, forgery, financial impropriety and alleged unlawful use of government facilities and official insignia. items.title: Coopération Guinée–Côte d’Ivoire : le PM Bah Oury conduit une forte délégation à Abidjan pour le 66ᵉ anniversaire de l’indépendance ivoirienne
items.description: Le Premier ministre, Amadou Oury Bah, a quitté Conakry à destination d'Abidjan pour représenter le Président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, aux festivités marquant le 66ᵉ anniversaire de l'indépendance de la République de Côte d'Ivoire, prévues les 6 et 7 août 2026. A travers cette mission de haut niveau, la Guinée réaffirme son attachement au renforcement de la coopération bilatérale, de l'intégration régionale et des liens historiques de fraternité qui unissent les peuples guinéen et ivoirien. Pour cette visite officielle, le Chef du Gouvernement est accompagné d'une importante délégation composée notamment du ministre des Affaires étrangères, de l'Intégration africaine et des Guinéens établis à l'étranger, Dr Morissanda Kouyaté, du ministre du Plan, de la Coopération internationale et du Développement, Ismaël Nabé, du ministre de la Modernisation de l'Administration et de la Fonction publique, Porte-parole du Gouvernement, François Bourouno, ainsi que du Directeur de Cabinet adjoint de la Primature et de plusieurs hauts cadres de l'administration publique. La participation de la Guinée revêt cette année un caractère particulier. Le pays figure en effet parmi les Etats invités d'honneur de cette célébration nationale, aux côtés de la République du Bénin, de la République gabonaise et de la République de l'Inde. Cette distinction traduit la qualité des relations diplomatiques entretenues entre Conakry et Abidjan ainsi que la volonté commune des deux Etats de consolider leur partenariat dans les domaines politique, économique, sécuritaire et culturel. Placées sous le thème « Forces de Défense et de Sécurité au service de la paix, de l'unité et du développement », les festivités du 66ᵉ anniversaire de l'indépendance ivoirienne réunissent plusieurs Chefs d'Etat, représentants gouvernementaux, délégations étrangères et partenaires internationaux autour d'un programme riche comprenant un défilé militaire et civil, des manifestations culturelles, des audiences officielles et des rencontres de haut niveau.

items.title: KMA to enforce standard container designs for all new structures in Kumasi from 2027
items.description: The Kumasi Metropolitan Chief Executive (MCE), Richard Ofori Agyemang Boadi, popularly known as ‘King Zuba,’ has announced the extension of the standardised prefabricated container design policy to other parts of Kumasi, especially areas where structures have been erected. Speaking to Joy News on the sidelines of the KMA General Assembly meeting, Mr Boadi said the initiative forms part of a broader city beautification programme. He said the pilot phase of the policy is currently underway around the Baba Yara Sports Stadium, aimed at bringing uniformity, order, and aesthetics to commercial structures across the metropolis. This comes amidst the Assembly’s demolition exercise, which occurred on July 31 around the Baba Yara Sports Stadium enclave, where occupants of unauthorised structures were directed to vacate the area as part of measures to improve sanitation, safety, and the general outlook of the city. “We will extend this standard to other parts of Kumasi where container structures have been mounted as and when we get there and deem it necessary to beautify the city,” he said. He also announced that from 2027, any individual or organisation seeking to mount a container structure within Kumasi will be required to obtain an approved standard design from the KMA before construction begins. According to him, the initiative is fully backed by the Assembly’s bye-law, having received endorsement from all Assembly members. “As part of our meeting, the assembly approved a motion that effective January 2027, anyone want to install a container in Kumasi must obtain a standard design from the KMA Spatial or Physical Planning Department,” Mr Boadi stated The mayor also disclosed plans to develop a well-organised trading structure at the Poku Trading Area to provide a more suitable environment for market women while enhancing the area’s appearance. “We have taken note of traders at the Poku Trading Area, particularly those who sell meat on the floor. We cannot continue to allow our market women to trade under such poor conditions. We will therefore provide trading structures for them at no cost. This project forms part of our commitment to create decent, well-structured spaces to make trading easier and safer for them and to beautify that part of the city. In a bid to tackle congestion, he said a major decongestion exercise will commence along a section of Alabar on August 17. “From August 17, we will begin a targeted decongestion exercise at Alabar. This is not about harassing traders. It is about restoring order, ensuring free movement of people and vehicles, and preventing avoidable accidents, he explained. The MCE described the move and other interventions as key to his administration’s vision of repositioning Kumasi as a cleaner, safer, and better-planned metropolis that reflects its historical importance.

items.title: “No ceremony can replace their voices” — Mahama consoles families of departed eight
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has assured the families of the eight Ghanaians who lost their lives in a helicopter crash on August 6, that the nation continues to share in their grief, saying their loved ones remain part of Ghana’s collective memory and will never be forgotten. President Mahama has expressed solidarity with the bereaved families of the eight fallen Ghanaian heroes, acknowledging their pain and assuring them that the entire nation continues to mourn with them. Speaking at the National Inter-Faith Memorial Service held in honour of the departed eight on August 6, President Mahama said the loss of their loved ones remains a painful moment for both the families and the country. He said no words, ceremonies or anniversaries could completely remove the pain of losing a cherished family member. “I know that no speech can erase your pain. No anniversary can fill that empty seat at your dining table. And no ceremonies can replace the voices that you long to hear or the embraces that you still miss,” he said. The President recognised the courage and dignity with which the families have carried their grief over the past year, saying their strength has been a source of inspiration to the nation. He said although death brings deep sorrow, the love shared with those who have passed continues through memories, faith and the lives they have influenced. “In doing so, you have reminded all of us that love does not end with death. It endures in memory, in faith, and in the lives we choose to live thereafter,” President Mahama said. He assured the families that they have not faced their loss alone, stressing that the sacrifices of their loved ones belong to the entire nation. “Please rest assured that the nation still mourns with you. Your loved ones did not die alone. They belong to all of Ghana, and Ghana will continue to remember them,” he said. President Mahama said the eight departed individuals represented dedication, patriotism and commitment to national duty, adding that their contributions will remain part of Ghana’s history. He also commended Ghanaians from all walks of life who supported the families through prayers, encouragement and acts of kindness following the tragedy. According to him, the support demonstrated the unity and compassion of Ghanaians beyond political, ethnic and religious differences. He urged the country to continue honouring the memory of the departed eight by upholding the values they represented — service, sacrifice, humility and commitment to the nation. The August 6, 2025 helicopter crash claimed the lives of Defence Minister Dr Edward Kofi Omane-Boamah, Agriculture Minister Dr Ibrahim Murtala Mohammed and six others, including three Ghana Air Force crew members, while they were travelling to the Ashanti Region in connection with the fight against illegal mining.

items.title: VeryDarkMan sets conditions for police appearance over AIG allegations
items.description: Social media activist Martins Otse, popularly known as VeryDarkMan, has agreed to honour the Nigeria Police Force’s invitation over allegations he made against the Assistant Inspector-General of Police (AIG) in charge of Zone 2 Command, Moshood Jimoh, but has requested that the process be transparent. VeryDarkMan’s position was conveyed in a statement issued by his lawyer, Deji Adeyanju, and shared on the activist’s Instagram page on Wednesday. The development follows an invitation from the police for VeryDarkMan to appear before the Force Criminal Investigation Department (FCID) in Abuja to provide evidence supporting his allegations against AIG Jimoh. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, had said on Tuesday that the police remained committed to due process, institutional discipline and the rule of law in handling the matter. The police also confirmed that AIG Jimoh had been invited by the FCID for questioning over the allegations, while VeryDarkMan received a formal invitation on July 30, 2026, to substantiate his claims. Responding to the invitation, VeryDarkMan’s legal team said the activist welcomed the investigation and remained ready to cooperate with the police. “Our client appreciates the decision of the Nigeria Police Force to commence an official investigation into the concerns he raised and reiterates his willingness to cooperate with the investigation. “For the avoidance of doubt, our client has never opposed any lawful investigation. On the contrary, he remains ready, willing and available to honour any invitation lawfully extended to him by the Nigeria Police Force,” the lawyers said. However, the legal team argued that the circumstances surrounding the allegations required an open and accountable process, particularly given the public interest in the matter and the senior position of the police officer involved. As a condition for VeryDarkMan’s appearance, his lawyers requested that representatives of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), civil society organisations and other independent observers be permitted to monitor the interview. “The interview must be observed by the civil society organisations, the Nigerian Bar Association and such other independent observers, as may be appropriate in the circumstances, to ensure maximum transparency and eliminate any possibility of misinformation or misrepresentation. “That his legal representative be permitted to accompany him and remain present throughout the interview.” Vanguard News The post VeryDarkMan sets conditions for police appearance over AIG allegations appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ADC’s Adio faults Presidency’s statement on EFCC, alleged court order over Osun accounts
items.description: LAGOS — House of Assembly candidate for Eti-Osa Constituency II, Ayodele Adio, has criticised a statement attributed to the Presidency directing the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) to vacate what it described as a court order suspending the accounts of the Osun State Government, describing the claim as misleading and legally untenable. In a statement issued on Thursday, Adio said there was no court order for the EFCC to vacate, arguing that the Presidency’s position reflected a misunderstanding of the law. He further maintained that even if such an order existed, the EFCC lacked the legal authority to set it aside. “There was no court order to vacate. More importantly, even if such an order existed, the EFCC has no legal authority to vacate or set aside a court order. Only a competent court can vary, discharge or vacate its own orders,” he said. Adio questioned the basis of the Presidency’s statement, arguing that it had created unnecessary confusion over an issue that should be governed strictly by the law. “What exactly is being presented to Nigerians? The rule of law cannot be replaced by public relations. Public institutions must operate within the limits of the law, not manufacture narratives that cannot withstand legal scrutiny,” he said. items.title: Two killed, seven injured in Mankessim–Accra Highway crash
items.description: Two people have died, and seven others have been injured following a road traffic accident at Abor Junction on the Mankessim–Accra Highway in the early hours of Thursday, August 6. The crash, involving a Toyota Voxy with registration number AS 8911-25, occurred shortly before 2:00 a.m., according to information released by the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS). According to GNFS, the Mankessim Fire Station received a distress call at 1:44 a.m., reporting the collision. Firefighters, supported by personnel from the National Ambulance Service, arrived at the scene at approximately 2:01 a.m. to carry out rescue operations. Emergency responders found nine occupants in the vehicle. Two of them—a man and a woman—had died by the time rescue teams arrived. The remaining seven occupants, comprising five men and two women, sustained injuries of varying severity and were attended to before being transported to health facilities for treatment. Three of the injured were taken to the Mercy Women Catholic Hospital in Mankessim for emergency medical care. The bodies of the deceased were conveyed to the Saltpond Government Hospital mortuary pending identification and further procedures. Authorities have not yet established what caused the accident, and investigations are expected to determine the circumstances surrounding the crash. The Fire Service said the driver of the vehicle escaped the accident without sustaining any injuries, although it remains unclear how the collision occurred. Following the rescue operation, firefighters removed debris from the roadway to restore normal traffic flow and prevent further accidents along the busy stretch of highway.

items.title: Football: Yan Diomandé au Real Madrid?
items.description: Selon The Athletic, le Real Madrid aurait conclu un accord avec le RB Leipzig pour le transfert de l'international ivoirien Yan Diomandé. L'opération, estimée à 125 millions d'euros auxquels pourraient s'ajouter 15 millions de bonus, ferait du jeune ailier de 19 ans l'une des recrues les plus onéreuses de l'histoire du football. Le Real Madrid serait sur le point de réaliser l'un des transferts les plus marquants de ce mercato estival. Selon The Athletic, le club madrilène aurait trouvé un terrain d'entente avec le RB Leipzig pour s'attacher les services de Yan Diomandé. Le montant de la transaction atteindrait 125 millions d'euros, auxquels pourraient s'ajouter 15 millions d'euros de bonus, portant la valeur totale du transfert à 140 millions d'euros. Si l'opération est officialisée, elle deviendrait le cinquième plus gros transfert de l'histoire du football et le plus important jamais réalisé par le Real Madrid, devant celui de Jude Bellingham, recruté en 2023 pour 127 millions d'euros. Âgé de 19 ans, l'ailier ivoirien se trouve actuellement en stage de préparation avec le RB Leipzig en Autriche. Toujours selon The Athletic, il ne manquerait plus que la validation définitive de l'accord par le club allemand avant que le joueur ne soit autorisé à rejoindre la capitale espagnole pour passer sa visite médicale. Un temps annoncé dans le viseur du Paris Saint-Germain, Yan Diomandé aurait finalement privilégié une arrivée au Real Madrid après le retrait du club parisien des discussions. L'international ivoirien sort d'une première saison convaincante sous les couleurs du RB Leipzig, avec un bilan de 13 buts et 10 passes décisives en 36 rencontres. Sous contrat jusqu'en 2030 avec le club allemand, il est considéré comme l'un des jeunes talents les plus prometteurs du football européen. À ce stade, le transfert n'a toutefois pas encore été officialisé par les deux clubs. Si les dernières étapes administratives sont franchies avec succès, Yan Diomandé s'apprête à franchir un cap majeur dans sa carrière en rejoignant le Real Madrid, dans le cadre d'une opération qui marquerait durablement l'histoire du marché des transferts. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Football: Yan Diomandé au Real Madrid? est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Reps Defence Committee hails Tinubu’s military pay rise, army expansion
items.description: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Defence, Hon. Babajimi Benson, has commended President Bola Tinubu for approving an upward review of salaries and welfare packages for personnel of the Armed Forces of Nigeria, describing the move as a major boost to the country’s security architecture. Benson also applauded the President’s approval for the expansion of the Nigerian Army from eight to 12 divisions through the creation of four new divisions in Makurdi, Ilorin, Jalingo and Benin City, alongside the recruitment of 28,000 additional personnel. In a statement issued on Thursday, the lawmaker described the decisions as “historic, visionary and timely interventions” that demonstrate the Federal Government’s commitment to strengthening national security and improving the welfare of military personnel. According to him, the improved remuneration, particularly the significant increase for junior personnel, would boost morale, enhance operational effectiveness, improve retention and attract qualified recruits into the Armed Forces. He stressed that prioritising the welfare of military personnel was crucial to building a disciplined and professional military capable of responding effectively to Nigeria’s evolving security challenges. Benson said the expansion of the Nigerian Army would enhance command and control, decentralise operational responsibilities, improve rapid troop deployment, strengthen border security and boost intelligence-led operations against terrorism, insurgency, banditry, kidnapping and other criminal activities. He added that the combination of improved welfare, increased manpower and enhanced operational structures would further strengthen Nigeria’s defence capabilities while promoting professionalism, discipline and institutional efficiency within the Armed Forces. “The President has once again demonstrated remarkable leadership and an unwavering commitment to the security and stability of our nation. These bold reforms represent strategic investments in the men and women who daily make enormous sacrifices to safeguard our country’s peace, unity and democratic values. “A well-motivated and properly equipped military remains indispensable to achieving sustainable national security and development,” Benson said. The committee chairman further stated that the reforms align with the objectives of President Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda and reflect the administration’s determination to build a modern, resilient and globally competitive military capable of addressing conventional and emerging security threats. He reaffirmed the commitment of the House Committee on Defence to supporting the reforms through legislative backing, policy support and effective oversight to ensure successful implementation. Benson expressed confidence that the measures would strengthen public trust in the Armed Forces, improve national security outcomes and contribute to lasting peace, stability and sustainable development across the country. Commenting on the development, the Managing Director of Cornerstone Insurance Plc, Stephen Alangbo, expressed his appreciation to the company’s stakeholders for their support in achieving this milestone. “We are pleased that Cornerstone Insurance Plc and FIN Insurance Company Limited have fulfilled the recapitalisation requirements under the Nigerian Insurance Industry Reform Act 2025. This achievement reinforces our financial strength and our capacity to continue bearing the risks entrusted to us and meeting our obligations to our numerous customers. “Innovation remains central to our approach, as we continue to develop solutions that respond to the evolving needs of our customers. The continued confidence and support of our partners, brokers and clients have been instrumental in achieving this important milestone, and we deeply appreciate their trust. “As we look ahead, we will invest further in technology to make our products and services more accessible and convenient, while continuously improving our overall customer experience. The public can be assured that Cornerstone Insurance Plc, together with its subsidiaries, FIN Insurance Company Limited and Hilal Takaful Insurance Limited, is well capitalised and strategically positioned to meet the evolving needs of our customers and stakeholders.” The fulfilment of the recapitalisation requirement strengthens the foundation upon which Cornerstone Insurance Plc and its subsidiaries will continue to serve customers and other stakeholders. For the Group, the milestone goes beyond meeting a regulatory requirement. It reflects a continued commitment to building resilient and dependable businesses with the capacity to take on risks and support customers when they need it most. The Group appreciates its customers, brokers, partners, shareholders and other stakeholders for their continued confidence, trust and support, which have been instrumental in achieving this important milestone. items.title: Otumfuo Osei Tutu II urges RCC Chief Directors to strengthen decentralisation and development delivery
items.description: The Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has charged Chief Directors of Regional Coordinating Councils (RCCs) to take responsibility for Ghana’s development agenda. He said that the success or failure of the country’s decentralisation policy lies squarely with them. Otumfuo made the remarks during a courtesy call by the Chief Directors at the Manhyia Palace. Addressing the delegation, the Asantehene noted that Chief Directors, as heads of the administrative structure in the regions, coordinate the work of all Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs) and therefore wield enormous influence over service delivery nationwide. “You are in charge of policies introduced by political leaders. Your office is the very foundation of decentralisation. If it fails to deliver on its purpose, you are to blame,” Otumfuo stated. “The politicians will come and go, but you remain in post. The continuity of government rests on your shoulders.” He urged the Chief Directors not to treat their positions as mere titles, but to translate their mandate into visible improvements in the lives of citizens. “Don’t regard the CD role as just a position. Let it translate into development,” he said. “How are you getting water, electricity and good roads to the places that need them? Politicians make promises on campaign platforms, but the realisation of those promises rests on you.” He noted that Ghanaians do not feel the impact of government policies in many communities because of weak coordination and lack of follow-through at the RCC and MMDA levels. Otumfuo further cautioned the administrators against silence in the face of poor decisions for fear of losing their jobs. “Make sure you give sound, professional advice to the political heads. You often fear telling them the truth because you fear losing your jobs, but you will be held accountable for keeping quiet,” he warned. He advised them to put their objections in writing where necessary. “If deaf ears are turned to your advice, document it for future reference. Think about Ghana first. Let us see the essence of decentralisation so that every corner of the country can taste and feel it,” Otumfuo added. The delegation was led by the Head of the Local Government Service, Prof. Lord Mensah, who was in Kumasi for training workshops for directors in the Ashanti Region. Prof. Mensah described Chief Directors as “the engine of governance” and assured the Asantehene that the Service had instituted measures to strengthen capacity, improve coordination, and ensure the smooth running of MMDAs across the country. The delegation included Felicia Dapaah Boakye, Chief Director of the Local Government Service; Lawyer Owusu Amoah, Chief Director of the Ashanti RCC; Jemima Lomotey of the Western North RCC; and S.S. Agbeve of the Oti RCC. Other members were Rachel Fosua of the Western RCC; Alhaji Avona Mohammed Akape of the Volta RCC; and Rev. Dr. Harry Kwatei Owoo of the Greater Accra RCC. Otumfuo offered his blessings to the delegation.

items.title: Benue Killings: 2Baba calls for urgent action, says ‘we can’t pretend anymore’
items.description: Nigerian music icon, Innocent Idibia, popularly known as 2Baba, has condemned the continued killings in Benue State, describing the attacks on communities in Otukpo Local Government Area as unacceptable. The Benue-born singer spoke on Wednesday during a visit to Otukpo-Nobi, one of the communities recently attacked by suspected armed herders. The visit came weeks after gunmen attacked the community on July 12, 2026, killing at least 10 residents and leaving several others injured. Sharing a video from the visit on his Instagram page, 2Baba said the pain of Benue residents was a collective concern, urging unity and commitment towards finding lasting solutions to the insecurity. “Benue is home. When home hurts, we all feel it. Today is about standing together, listening, and reminding one another that hope is never lost,” he wrote. Addressing residents of the affected community, the singer expressed sympathy with victims and their families, while calling on stakeholders to work together to end the recurring violence. He lamented the rising cases of bloodshed in the state, saying the situation had become too serious to be ignored. “It’s becoming too much now, we can’t pretend anymore. We need to begin planning. It won’t be automatic, but there is definitely going to be a solution,” 2Baba said. The music star stressed that resolving the security challenges would require the collective efforts of government, communities and other stakeholders. “It’s not going to be one person, we all need to come together and fight it. I came to sympathise with you all. It’s painful,” he added. The post Benue Killings: 2Baba calls for urgent action, says ‘we can’t pretend anymore’ appeared first on Vanguard News .
