items.title: Mahama urges reforms to honour fallen helicopter victims
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has called on leaders at every level of public service to honour the memory of the eight Ghanaians who perished in last year’s military helicopter crash by building stronger institutions, improving safety standards and placing the welfare of public servants at the centre of governance. Addressing the National Inter-Faith Memorial Service in Accra on Thursday, August 6, to commemorate the first anniversary of the tragedy, the President said the most enduring tribute the nation could pay to those who died was not the erection of monuments, but the pursuit of responsible leadership and meaningful institutional reforms. Speaking before bereaved families, religious leaders, members of the diplomatic corps, traditional authorities, security chiefs and government officials, President Mahama described public office as “a sacred trust” and urged those entrusted with authority never to lose sight of the human consequences of their decisions. “Today should also be a moment of reflection for all of us who are entrusted with leadership, that every decision we make affects lives,” he said. “Every public office is ultimately a sacred trust. Leadership is not measured merely by the authority we exercise, but by the responsibility we bear for the lives and welfare of those who serve our nation.” The President said the deaths of the eight public servants imposed a lasting obligation on the country to ensure that lessons learnt from the tragedy lead to tangible improvements in governance and public administration. “Their memory therefore imposes upon us a solemn obligation to build stronger institutions, to strengthen safety standards wherever necessary, to invest in the welfare of our personnel, and to ensure that no lesson from this tragedy will ever be forgotten,” he stated. President Mahama stressed that remembrance should not end with annual ceremonies but should inspire concrete action that protects those who continue to serve Ghana. “The greatest memorial we can build is not one made of stone or bronze,” he declared. “It is one that is built through responsible leadership, improved systems and a steadfast commitment to protecting those who dedicate their lives to Ghana.” He noted that governments have a duty to continually review operational procedures, strengthen institutional resilience and provide adequate support for personnel whose work often exposes them to significant risks in the service of the nation. According to him, the true legacy of the eight departed public servants would be realised only if Ghana emerged from the tragedy with stronger institutions, enhanced safety protocols and a renewed commitment to safeguarding those who dedicate their lives to public service. Reflecting on the significance of the inter-faith memorial service, President Mahama said Ghanaians, regardless of their religious beliefs, shared a common conviction that death is not the end of life’s journey. “My fellow citizens, our faith teaches us that death is not the end,” he said. “Whether we are Christian or Muslim, whether guided by traditional beliefs or by another form of faith, we all hold on to the conviction that every life has a meaning beyond the years we count on it.” He said the gathering symbolised the unity that exists among Ghanaians despite differences in religion and culture. “That is why we have gathered today in an inter-faith service. We come from different traditions, but we lift one prayer. We come with different expressions of worship, but with one shared hope.” The President prayed that God would grant eternal peace to the departed and continue to comfort the families they left behind. “We pray that the Almighty God, in His infinite mercy, has welcomed our departed brothers into eternal peace. We pray that He continues to comfort every grieving family, and we pray for the wisdom to live lives that are worthy of the opportunities He has granted to us.” President Mahama urged Ghanaians not to leave the memorial service burdened only by sorrow but inspired to build a nation worthy of the sacrifices made by the deceased. “As we leave this memorial service today, let us carry with us not only sadness but also a sense of purpose,” he said. He challenged citizens and public officials alike to honour the fallen through integrity, selflessness and compassion. “Let us honour the departed by serving our nation with greater integrity. Let us honour them by placing duty above self-interest. Let us honour them by treating one another with greater kindness.” He added that the country should strive to create a society in which every citizen feels valued and every act of service is recognised. “Let us honour them by building a Ghana where every citizen feels that their service matters and every sacrifice is remembered.” Acknowledging that grief remains a daily reality for many of the bereaved families, the President said the passage of time had not diminished the nation’s gratitude. “One year has passed. The pain may have softened for some, but it remains raw for others. Our remembrance endures.” He said the eight victims would forever occupy a unique place in Ghana’s history because of the dedication with which they served the nation. “The names of these eight faithful servants will forever occupy a special place in the story of our nation, not because of the manner in which they died, but because of the spirit with which they lived and served God and country.” On 6th August, 2025, Ghana suffered one of its gravest national tragedies when a Ghana Armed Forces helicopter crashed during an official assignment, killing all eight people on board. The victims included senior government officials, national security personnel and military officers who were travelling in the line of duty. The accident sent shockwaves across the country and prompted a period of national mourning. Tributes poured in from political leaders across the divide, civil society organisations, religious bodies and ordinary citizens, all paying tribute to individuals who had devoted their lives to the service of Ghana.

items.title: Géopolitique de l’arme nucléaire
items.description: L’arme nucléaire est un élément central des relations internationales et un enjeu majeur de sécurité et de dissuasion. À ce jour, neuf États possèdent l’arme nucléaire : les États-Unis, la Russie, la France, le Royaume-Uni, la Chine, l’Inde, le Pakistan, Israël et la Corée du Nord. Le Traité sur la non-prolifération des armes nucléaires (TNP), signé en 1968, vise à limiter la diffusion de cette arme et à favoriser le désarmement. Toutefois, son efficacité reste limitée puisque certains États n’y ont jamais adhéré et que d’autres s’en sont retirés. Les conflits récents illustrent l’importance stratégique de l’arme nucléaire, qui constitue pour certains États une garantie contre toute intervention militaire extérieure et un moyen d'assurer la survie de leur régime. Les frappes menées par Israël et les États-Unis contre des installations nucléaires iraniennes ont ravivé les inquiétudes liées au risque de prolifération nucléaire. En quoi le risque de prolifération constitue-t-il un enjeu majeur pour la sécurité internationale ? Un désarmement nucléaire est-il encore envisageable dans le contexte géopolitique actuel ? L’article Géopolitique de l’arme nucléaire est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — VICE President Kashim Shettima on Thursday commenced a two-week leave. Senior Special Assistant to the President on media and communications, Mr. Stanley Nkwocha, said the leave was the first one the Vice President was embarking on since 2023 he was sworn into office. The statement read: “Following the approval by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, Vice President Kashim Shettima will begin a two-week leave on Thursday, August 6, 2026 – his first since being sworn into office. “During the period, the Vice President will devote time to study, reflection and intellectual renewal as part of efforts to strengthen his capacity for continued service to the nation. “The leave offers Senator Shettima an opportunity to review the administration’s ongoing programmes, deepen his understanding of emerging national and global policy issues, and prepare for the responsibilities ahead as the Federal Government intensifies the implementation of the Renewed Hope Agenda. “Since assuming office on May 29, 2023, the Vice President has remained actively engaged in the coordination and supervision of several strategic government initiatives, particularly in economic development, food security, humanitarian affairs, digital transformation, job creation and regional cooperation. “He has also chaired the National Economic Council, which brings together the governors of the 36 states, the Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria and other relevant public officials to deliberate on policies affecting the economy and the welfare of Nigerians. “Beyond his responsibilities within the country, Vice President Shettima has represented President Tinubu at major international and regional engagements, advancing Nigeria’s position on economic integration, peace and security, climate action, investment and sustainable development. “Senator Shettima remains deeply committed to the ideals of loyalty, duty and service that have defined his role in the administration, as well as to supporting President Tinubu’s efforts to build a more secure, productive and prosperous Nigeria.” The statement added: “The Vice President will return to office at the end of the two-week leave period and resume his official responsibilities with renewed energy and dedication to the service of the nation.” The post Shettima begins 2-week leave, pledges renewed commitment to national service appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Opération Marhaba 2026 : Bab Moulay Driss s'inscrit dans la dynamique nationale en faveur des Marocains du Monde
items.description: À l'occasion de l'Opération Marhaba 2026, Bab Moulay Driss a pris part à la mobilisation nationale en faveur des Marocains Résidant à l'Étranger (MRE) en lançant une initiative d'accueil au Port Tanger Med, marquant ainsi son engagement en faveur des valeurs d'hospitalité, de solidarité et d'attachement qui caractérisent le Royaume du Maroc. Cette initiative s'inscrit dans la continuité de la Haute Sollicitude que Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI, que Dieu L'Assiste, n'a cessé d'accorder aux Marocains Résidant à l'Étranger. À travers Ses Hautes Orientations, le Souverain œuvre au renforcement des dispositifs d'accueil, d'accompagnement et de proximité destinés aux MRE, tout en réaffirmant leur rôle essentiel dans le développement économique, social et le rayonnement international du Royaume. Chaque année, l'Opération Marhaba constitue l'un des plus importants dispositifs d'accueil des Marocains du Monde. Au-delà de sa dimension humaine et familiale, elle représente un moment fort de la vie nationale, favorisant les échanges, le tourisme, l'investissement et la consommation, tout en consolidant les liens entre la diaspora marocaine et son pays d'origine. Consciente de l'importance de ce rendez-vous national, Bab Moulay Driss a souhaité apporter sa contribution à cet élan collectif en accueillant les Marocains du Monde dès leur arrivée au Royaume. À cette occasion, plus de 6 000 coffrets de bienvenue ont été remis aux voyageurs, dans un esprit de partage et de transmission des traditions marocaines. Inspirés du patrimoine culturel national, ces coffrets ont été conçus comme un geste symbolique reflétant l'art de vivre marocain et les valeurs d'accueil qui font la renommée du Royaume. À travers cette initiative, Bab Moulay Driss entend célébrer le lien indéfectible qui unit les Marocains du Monde à leur terre d'origine et contribuer, à son échelle, à l'expérience d'accueil qui leur est réservée. Abdesselam El Alami, Fondateur de Bab Moulay Driss : « Les Marocains du Monde occupent une place essentielle dans le cœur de tous les Marocains et contribuent, chaque jour, au développement et au rayonnement de notre pays. À travers cette initiative, nous avons souhaité leur réserver un accueil inspiré de nos traditions, en nous inscrivant dans la dynamique nationale portée sous l'impulsion de Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI, que Dieu L'Assiste. » Au-delà de cette action, Bab Moulay Driss réaffirme sa volonté d'accompagner les initiatives qui valorisent le patrimoine marocain et renforcent le sentiment d'appartenance des Marocains à leur identité, où qu'ils résident dans le monde. Convaincue que les entreprises ont également un rôle à jouer dans la promotion des valeurs du Royaume, la Maison poursuit son engagement en faveur de projets porteurs de sens, au service du patrimoine, de la culture et du rayonnement du Maroc. Abdesselam El Alami, Fondateur de Bab Moulay Driss : « Notre ambition est de faire vivre le patrimoine marocain à travers des initiatives qui créent du lien, transmettent notre héritage et mettent en lumière l'authenticité du Maroc. Accueillir les Marocains du Monde est une manière de leur témoigner notre reconnaissance et de célébrer leur attachement indéfectible à leur pays. » The post Opération Marhaba 2026 : Bab Moulay Driss s'inscrit dans la dynamique nationale en faveur des Marocains du Monde appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Osun Election: ICPC deploys operatives to 30 LGs, warns against vote buying
items.description: The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) has announced plans to deploy its operatives across all the 30 local government areas of Osun State to monitor the August 15 governorship election and tackle vote buying. The Resident Anti-Corruption Commissioner for Osun State, Yusuf Olatunji, disclosed this on Thursday while speaking with journalists during a street rally organised by the commission in Osogbo to sensitise residents against electoral corruption. The rally, which was aimed at discouraging vote trading ahead of the election, attracted corps members, officials of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), ICPC personnel and other stakeholders. Participants moved from Igbona Market through Old Garage and Olaiya areas before terminating the procession at Alekuwodo Market, Osogbo. During the exercise, speakers used major Nigerian languages to educate residents on the dangers of vote buying, while fliers containing information on the consequences of the practice were distributed to members of the public. Addressing journalists after the rally, Olatunji said the campaign was part of the commission’s efforts to raise awareness about the illegality of buying and selling votes. “We are out here to let the people of the state know that vote buying is a crime under Nigerian law. From the ICPC, we will not tolerate vote buying or selling, and anybody culpable will be arrested and prosecuted,” he said. The ICPC official disclosed that the commission had concluded arrangements to deploy personnel across all local government areas in the state to monitor the electoral process and prevent attempts to compromise voters. “The Commission has made adequate arrangements to deploy our personnel to all the 30 local governments to monitor the election to ensure that vote buying is eradicated. “We want to appeal to voters that they should not encourage vote buying. Do not allow anybody to deceive you with money. Anybody involved in such an act — both the giver and the receiver — is liable and will be punished,” Olatunji warned. He urged voters to protect the integrity of the electoral process by rejecting all forms of electoral corruption, particularly vote buying and vote selling. According to him, while exchanging votes for money may provide temporary financial relief, it causes long-term damage to democracy by turning leadership into a transaction rather than a public mandate. “Vote buying and vote selling may appear to offer temporary financial relief, but they inflict lasting damage on our democracy. When votes become commodities, leadership becomes a transaction rather than a mandate,” he said. Olatunji noted that the consequences of electoral corruption include poor governance, unfulfilled promises, inadequate infrastructure, insecurity, unemployment and declining public confidence in democratic institutions. He advised voters to consider the long-term impact of their electoral choices, stressing that money received during elections cannot compensate for the consequences of electing leaders who fail to deliver quality education, healthcare, infrastructure, employment opportunities and sustainable development. The ICPC’s sensitisation campaign comes ahead of the Osun governorship election scheduled for August 15. items.title: Nigerian author Jerry Falade loses $2m book deal over AI allegations
items.description: Nigerian author Jerry Falade has lost a reported $2 million publishing deal for his debut crime novel after concerns emerged over whether artificial intelligence (AI) was used in the writing or editing process. Falade’s highly anticipated novel, Call Me, I’ll Hide the Body , was withdrawn from sale by his literary agents despite reportedly attracting an offer of more than $2 million from Minotaur, an imprint of Macmillan US. The deal was reportedly secured after a 14-way auction, with the novel initially scheduled for publication in 2028. In the UK, the manuscript also attracted several six-figure bids through a competitive publishing process. In an email to publishers, Falade’s agents said they could no longer verify how the manuscript had developed from its original concept to its completed form. “Jerry Falade produced an incredible manuscript that dazzled us and the top publishing professionals around the world. Unfortunately, we are no longer able to authenticate how the manuscript fully evolved from origin to completion.” The agents said they had previously discussed AI use with Falade during the submission process and accepted his assurance that the technology had not been used as a writing or editorial resource. “During the submission process we vetted the manuscript with Jerry for AI and felt trusting in his reassurance that it was written without utilising AI as a resource in the writing or editorial process. We can no longer substantiate that, and we are withdrawing the book.” Falade’s US agent, Marc Gerald of Europa Content, told the Bookseller that he first read the manuscript in June and was immediately impressed by its quality. Gerald described the book as “stunningly good, everyone fell in love with it. It’s a book that appeals to absolutely everyone.” However, he said an editor raised concerns about possible AI use halfway through the submission process. Gerald said Europa Content decided against using AI-detection software to examine the manuscript because Falade had provided what he considered a “clear and credible” explanation. The agency later decided to sever ties with Falade following a meeting on July 29, when, according to Gerald, “aspects of [Falade’s] story changed”. Gerald said the agency’s decision was based on its “need to have total faith” in the author. He also maintained that the quality of the manuscript itself was not in question. “We feel terrible for putting this into the universe and the firestorm it has caused,” Gerald said. “The book itself is genius – however it came to be drafted, it’s amazing.” Falade has rejected allegations that he used AI and accused the publishing industry of racial bias in its response to the controversy. In a statement, he said: “Three Black authors received major publishing deals this year, and all three later had deals cancelled or disrupted following suspicions about AI. There seems to be a troubling assumption that when a Black writer produces work that attracts significant attention, the work could not possibly be their own. Meanwhile, there are popular white writers who have publicly mentioned using AI for their writing processes and they’re still doing fine.” Falade did not name the other authors he referenced, but two Black US authors, Mia Ballard and HM Wolfe, have faced similar AI allegations this year. Both have denied using AI. Ballard’s horror novel Shy Girl had its US release withdrawn by Hachette after online rumours that she had relied on AI, allegations she denied. Falade said his own situation escalated quickly after rumours began circulating. “In my case, rumours began circulating and, within six hours, I had been dropped by my agency, deals were paused, and press releases were being issued.” He also questioned the reliability of AI-detection software, saying such tools “are widely known to produce false positives”. Falade argued that the manuscript had already been scrutinised by several publishing professionals before attracting major offers. He said the novel had “passed through first readers, second readers, editors, and acquisitions teams at numerous publishing houses … If the manuscript had shown genuine signs of being generated by AI, it is difficult to believe that every one of those experienced professionals would have failed to notice.” The controversy comes as the publishing industry continues to grapple with the growing use of AI in creative writing and questions over how publishers should verify the origins of manuscripts. items.title: “His laughter still lives with us” — Widow remembers Flight Sergeant Addo Mensah at crash memorial
items.description: The wife of the late Flight Sergeant Ernest Addo Mensah has paid an emotional tribute to her husband and the seven other victims of the August 6, 2025, military helicopter crash, saying the pain of losing them remains as deep today as it was a year ago. Speaking on behalf of her family at the National Inter-Faith Memorial Service held at the University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA) on Thursday, August 6, she described the past 12 months as a difficult period marked by grief, reflection and healing. She said the tragedy had left an irreplaceable void in the family, noting that they had lost not only a husband, son and brother, but also someone whose optimism and warmth brought joy to everyone around him. “We stand here today with hearts that still remember, still mourn and still honour the life of our beloved husband, son and brother, Flight Sergeant Ernest Addo Mensah. “Today, we stand 12 months removed from a tragedy that still feels painfully near. A day that completely altered our lives as a family. “I, for one, have never known a person more optimistic than Ernest. You could hardly remain sad around him. He would crack jokes and laugh at them more than you would. And before long, you would find yourself smiling and forgetting the burden that had troubled you.” She said the family had drawn strength from the support of friends, colleagues and well-wishers throughout the past year. She also expressed gratitude to President John Dramani Mahama for honouring the memory of the victims and supporting the bereaved families, as well as to the Ghana Armed Forces for its continued care and assistance. “As we honour the memory of the eight fallen heroes, we choose to remember not the tragedy that took them from us, but the lives they lived, the love they had for their families, their dedication to duty and the values they carried with honour,” she said, urging Ghanaians to uphold the values of service, sacrifice and compassion exemplified by the deceased. The memorial service brought together government officials, religious leaders, traditional authorities, members of the Ghana Armed Forces, bereaved families and other dignitaries to commemorate the first anniversary of the crash. The eight victims died on August 6, 2025, when a Ghana Armed Forces Z-9 helicopter crashed in the Adansi Akrofuom District of the Ashanti Region while on an official assignment from Accra. It formed part of activities marking the first anniversary of one of Ghana’s worst aviation disasters.

items.title: India's Modi turns to Instagram to woo young voters after Gen Z protest
items.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi took to Instagram recently with selfie-style videos shot after hours in a bid to win over young voters following Gen Z protests that highlighted growing frustration over a lack of job and education opportunities. From clips showing the prime minister in a biker jacket and sunglasses against a rap soundtrack, to others that borrow the theme song from the sitcom Friends to signal his dependability, the messaging of Modi’s party has pivoted towards the young. A vertically shot clip posted on July 31 featuring Modi uttering a casual greeting, “Hi, friends” was the latest in his digital charm offensive that aims to win over 400 million Gen Z voters ahead of general elections in 2029. “They are platforms where you broadcast a well-rehearsed and disciplined political message to millions of followers in a top-down manner,” said Delhi-based political columnist Asim Ali. The pivot to youth-focused social media follows protests last month that led to the resignation of the education minister after tens of thousands of students and job seekers took to the streets. The outcry was triggered by a leaked examination paper in a country where such tests are seen as opening the gates to professional careers and eventual financial security. Ministers, government departments issue clips Modi’s videos have spurred cabinet ministers and government departments to issue a stream of short, lightly edited clips online over the past 10 days, with the foreign ministry becoming the latest on Thursday, saying it will take to Snapchat. Since sweeping to power in 2014, Modi has been credited with transforming political communication in India, using digital platforms to build a direct connection with voters. Analysts say his ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) also developed a highly effective communications network across television news channels and social media platforms such as WhatsApp and X. But platforms such as Instagram reward spontaneity, humour and authenticity over tightly scripted messaging, said Ali. That is where the protesters scored, amplifying their message with Instagram reels and short videos that challenged Modi’s carefully cultivated image of political invincibility and his government’s command of the public narrative. The BJP’s earlier digital outreach felt too manicured to attract young audiences who preferred raw and unedited content instead, other analysts said. “Content that feels too carefully curated, where the words are measured, the look is staid and the background feels staged, is less likely to be appealing,” said Joyojeet Pal, a professor at Michigan University’s information school. Eye on 2029 general election Experts say the BJP’s renewed outreach reflects the growing political importance of younger voters. More than half of India’s population of 1.4 billion consists of those younger than 35, and Gen Z is expected to form one of the largest voting blocs by the time the general election is held in 2029, which could give Modi a fourth term in office. Amit Malviya, the BJP’s social media chief, declined to comment and queries sent to four national party spokespersons went unanswered. The party is also stepping up efforts beyond social media, with plans for an address on Thursday to about 2,000 students in the financial capital of Mumbai by Mohan Bhagwat, the chief of its ideological parent , the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). That represents one of the parent group’s biggest efforts to engage with the Gen Z young. At a cabinet meeting after the protests, Modi urged ministers to be more active on platforms popular with the young and make sure their videos appeared less polished. “Earlier, there were a lot more static posts tailored to X or Facebook,” said a member of the communications team of a BJP minister, speaking on condition of anonymity. “But now the ask is for more reels, preferably with minimal editing and some rawness.” Posters of Gen Z pledges Posters proclaiming “I am Gen Z” have sprung up across Mumbai, bearing pledges attributed to Gen Z, from promises to respect the police, the army and Modi, as well as support students. It is unclear if the strategy will succeed, however. “The internet has its own language and culture,” said author and podcaster Anurag Minus Verma. “Serious political messaging, packaged as reels, can still be trolled. There will be more focus on Instagram, but it remains to be seen if Gen Z buys into that.”

items.title: Osun Election: Makinde condemns EFCC account freeze, warns against political use of institutions
items.description: Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has condemned the reported freezing of the Osun State Government’s account by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), alleging that the action was part of a pattern of using federal institutions to disrupt governance in opposition-controlled states. Makinde stated this in a message posted on his official X handle on Thursday, insisting that while no government or public office holder should be above scrutiny, law enforcement agencies must operate with fairness, professionalism and political neutrality. The EFCC had reportedly obtained a court order freezing Osun State Government accounts days before the state’s governorship election. Reacting to the development, Makinde said the use of institutions such as the EFCC to target specific states or individuals could undermine public confidence in such agencies. “As I said in my last newsletter, no government is above scrutiny, but when institutions like the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) are utilised to witch-hunt specific states or public office holders, it indicates that their investigations are selective and erodes public trust in these institutions,” he said. The governor argued that freezing an official state government account without due legal process exceeded the powers granted to the EFCC under Nigerian law. He also questioned the timing of the action, suggesting that it could influence the outcome of the forthcoming Osun governorship election. “The timing of the action suggests that this is just another attempt by the Federal Government to unduly influence the forthcoming governorship election in Osun State,” Makinde stated. He called on federal institutions to remain faithful to their constitutional responsibilities by ensuring fairness, professionalism and political neutrality in the discharge of their duties. Makinde also urged Nigerians, civil society organisations and the international community to remain vigilant, warning that democracy cannot thrive where institutions are perceived as tools for political intimidation. “Protecting the independence and credibility of our institutions is essential to preserving public trust and safeguarding Nigeria’s democracy. The rule of law must prevail over the rule of politics,” he added. items.title: ‘No more a death sentence’: Upper West gets expanded dialysis unit after years of pain, pleadings and hope
items.description: For years, a kidney failure diagnosis in the Upper West Region was almost a death sentence. Not because the disease was untreatable. But because the treatment – dialysis – was 700km away in Accra or Kumasi. Families sold everything. Patients were airlifted. Others simply died on the road. That painful chapter ended in Wa on Tuesday, August 4. At the official commissioning of the new dialysis unit at the Upper West Regional Hospital, the Medical Director of the Upper West Regional Hospital, Dr. (Med.) Philip K. K. Baabiineh, could not hold back. “As a doctor, I have witnessed patients with kidney failure deteriorate before my eyes. Not because their disease was untreatable but because dialysis, the very treatment that could sustain their life, was inaccessible,” he said. “I have watched families exhaust every resource searching for dialysis outside the region. I have watched hope fade from their eyes. Those moments no healthcare professional will forever forget.” Before 2022, he added, patients who couldn’t afford the trip were “often left to their fate”. Dr Baabiineh warned that “persistent power fluctuations” pose “a serious risk to the longevity and reliability of these sophisticated dialysis machines”. “We therefore respectfully appeal to all stakeholders… to support efforts aimed at ensuring a stable and uninterrupted power supply to this hospital. Protecting these machines is ultimately protecting the lives of the patients who depend on them. The man who made it happen is Rt. Hon. Alban Bagbin, Speaker of Parliament. Speaking at the event, the former Nadowli-Kaleo MP recounted how he personally airlifted patients to Accra for dialysis treatment. “I have personally airlifted some patients from the region at great cost to acquire dialysis treatment, only for them to die. This year, last year, I experienced it. And some of their parents are here. They can attest to it. So as a nation we can never be comfortable with this reality. He added, “Today we respond not with words alone but with deeds and real action. With the support of the Upper West Parliamentary Caucus, my members always behind me, representing you, even though now I represent the whole country, and the facilitation of SHEILD, I am honoured to support the expansion of services at this hospital through the donation of these six dialysis machines and recliners. They are not refurbished… they are brand new, tear rubber,” he emphasised. But the cost was too high. So he partnered with health NGO Sustainable Health Education and Interventions Limited (SHEILD) and donors to bring six dialysis machines. SHEILD Board Director Dr. John Nkrumah Mills, though excited about the intervention, believes that more needs to be done. ‘‘The project was to provide six modern machines, which would take care of the patients. That is expanding the capacity already and then improving the care. We started in January this year, and we are commissioning it today. I must say I was surprised when I got in. I think we may have to increase our machine load because already six patients are being dialysed at the moment. This wasn’t intentional as a demonstration. Six patients are being dialysed today. What it means is that we can do dialysis 12 times in a 24-hour cycle, if that’s what it’s to be,” he explained. “It’s a lifesaving intervention. Dialysis was something we could only hear of at Korle Bu. Today, listening to the cries and the pleas of the people, he (Speaker Bagbin) has brought this intervention.” Board Director of SHEILD, Dr. Sylvie Anie, said the organisation remains committed to addressing critical healthcare gaps through sustainable interventions that improve lives. “This expanded dialysis unit represents far more than additional equipment or infrastructure. It represents hope for patients and families who have struggled for years to access specialised kidney care. Our vision is to ensure that quality healthcare becomes more accessible, more equitable and more sustainable for every Ghanaian.” She stated that the initiative aligns with SHEILD’s mission of promoting health education, strengthening healthcare systems and supporting interventions that deliver lasting public health impact. Naa Professor Edmund Nminyem Delle Chiir VIII, Paramount Chief of Nandom, a renowned Ghanaian dermatologist, spoke for traditional leaders. “This dialysis centre that we are commissioning today is a dream come true for the people of this region,” he said. “For years our people have suffered. They have travelled long distances to Accra, to Kumasi, and many have died on the way… Today, that story has changed.” But Professor Delle had another plea: housing for doctors. “We now have about 250 of our boys from Nandom who are now doctors. But why don’t they come to help us? It’s because of the lack of facilities… We don’t have quarters for the doctors. We don’t have quarters for the nurses.” Leader of the Upper West Parliamentary caucus, Dr. Sebastian Sandaare, said the centre was the result of years of advocacy. “People have suffered. People have died… just because of lack of dialysis services in this region. Today we are happy that this dream has finally materialised. No longer will our people have to travel to Accra or Kumasi.” Speaking on behalf of the Regional Minister, Chief Director Pognaa Fati Issaka Koray called it “a significant milestone” that will “reduce inequalities in access to essential medical services” and give “renewed hope to patients living with kidney disease”.

items.title: ‘Life is fragile, service is sacred’ – Mahama reflects on helicopter crash victims one year on
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has described the loss of the eight Ghanaian servicemen who died in a helicopter crash as a painful reminder that life is fragile, service to the nation is sacred and tomorrow is never guaranteed. He said their dedication to duty and commitment to Ghana must remain a lasting inspiration for the country. Speaking at the National Inter-Faith Memorial Service held in honour of the departed eight on August 6, President Mahama said the occasion was not only a moment to mourn but also an opportunity to give meaning to the lives they lived and the sacrifices they made. “Today is one of those days when a nation deliberately slows its pace, not because history demands it, but because memory does,” he said. The President recalled that one year earlier, Ghana woke up to the devastating news of the helicopter accident that claimed eight precious lives while they were on national duty. He said the tragedy went beyond individual families and became a moment of national grief. “Some tragedies unfold quietly within families and communities. Then some tragedies touch the conscience of an entire nation. And this was one such tragedy,” President Mahama said. He described the moment Ghanaians received the news as one filled with disbelief, grief and unanswered questions, noting that many people could still remember exactly where they were when they heard of the incident. The President said the greatest lesson from the tragedy is that life must be valued because “life is fragile, service is sacred, and tomorrow can never be guaranteed.” President Mahama acknowledged the pain suffered by parents who lost their children, spouses who lost lifelong partners, children who lost their fathers, and colleagues who lost trusted friends and comrades. However, he said the memorial service was not only about remembering the painful circumstances surrounding their deaths but also about celebrating the values they represented. “Remembrance is an obligation for every grateful nation,” he said. According to him, a country that forgets those who served it risks forgetting the principles and values upon which it was built. He said the lives of the eight departed individuals demonstrated that sacrifice matters, service deserves honour and those who dedicate themselves to the nation will never disappear from history. President Mahama noted that although the eight came from different backgrounds, professions and personal experiences, they were united by one common purpose — answering the call to serve God and country. He said none of them boarded the helicopter knowing it would be their final journey. “They left behind unfinished conversations, appointments they expected to keep, families they expected to return to, and dreams they believed they still had time to fulfil,” he said. Reflecting on the work of public servants, President Mahama said many men and women dedicate their lives to Ghana by working under difficult conditions, spending long periods away from their families and making decisions under pressure. He said these sacrifices often go unnoticed because many public servants carry out their duties quietly and without recognition. President Mahama said moments of tragedy test not only a nation’s institutions but also its humanity, and Ghana’s response showed the strength of its collective spirit. He concluded by urging Ghanaians to continue honouring the memory of the departed eight by upholding the values of service, sacrifice, compassion and unity that defined their lives. The August 6, 2025 helicopter crash claimed the lives of Defence Minister Dr Edward Kofi Omane-Boamah, Agriculture Minister Dr Ibrahim Murtala Mohammed and six others, including three Ghana Air Force crew members, while they were travelling to the Ashanti Region in connection with the fight against illegal mining.

items.title: Burkina/Master: Dieudonné Sawadogo analyse la mobilisation des terres rurales pour cause d’utilité publique dans la vallée de Samendéni
items.description: BURKINA-SOUTENANCE-MASTER-GOUVERNANCE-FONCIERE-VALLEE-SAMENDENI Burkina/Master: Dieudonné Sawadogo analyse la mobilisation des terres rurales pour cause d’utilité publique dans la vallée de Samendéni Ouagadougou, 6 août 2026 (AIB) – L’inspecteur des Eaux et Forêts, Dieudonné Sawadogo, a soutenu, le 29 juillet 2026 à l’Université Nazi Boni, son mémoire de fin de cycle pour l’obtention du diplôme de Master en développement rural et gouvernance foncière, sur le thème : « Analyse des conditions et procédures de mobilisation des terres rurales pour cause d’utilité publique : cas du Programme de développement intégré de la vallée de Samendéni (PDIS), Burkina Faso ». Le jury lui a décerné la note de 17,5/20, avec la mention Très bien. L’inspecteur des Eaux et Forêts, a indiqué que l’étude a couvert la période de mise en œuvre du programme allant de 2007 à 2021. Il a expliqué qu’elle a combiné une recherche documentaire et une collecte de données auprès des différents acteurs concernés, afin d’apprécier les conditions de mobilisation foncière et leurs effets sur les populations affectées. Selon les résultats présentés par l’impétrant, les procédures administratives prévues par la Réorganisation agraire et foncière (RAF), ainsi que les normes environnementales et sociales de la Banque mondiale, ont été respectées dans la mise en œuvre du PDIS. Il a cependant souligné que certains engagements prévus dans le Plan de gestion environnementale et sociale (PGES) en faveur des populations affectées n’ont pas été totalement honorés. M. Sawadogo a néanmoins relevé plusieurs acquis, notamment l’indemnisation de certains biens, l’aide à la réinstallation des populations, ainsi que la réalisation d’infrastructures sociales de base, dont des centres de santé, des écoles et des points d’eau. Il a également précisé que la mise en œuvre du PDIS a favorisé le développement de nouvelles activités, notamment la pêche et le tourisme dans la zone concernée. Face aux insuffisances constatées, l’inspecteur des Eaux et Forêts recommande aux projets et programmes de respecter pleinement les engagements contenus dans les PGES. Il préconise aussi à l’État d’actualiser les barèmes d’indemnisation des espèces agricoles et forestières en prenant en compte leur valeur écosystémique. Dieudonné Sawadogo a, en outre, recommandé un accompagnement des personnes affectées jusqu’à leur réinsertion socio-économique complète, afin de mieux prendre en compte les conséquences sociales et économiques des mobilisations foncières pour cause d’utilité publique. Les membres du jury ont salué la pertinence et la qualité de ce travail de recherche en lui attribuant la note de 17,5/20, avec la mention Très bien. Ils ont également formulé des amendements afin de parfaire le document. Cette recherche contribue à améliorer la gouvernance des terres rurales mobilisées pour cause d’utilité publique, en mettant l’accent sur le respect des engagements envers les populations affectées et l’amélioration des mécanismes d’indemnisation. Ses recommandations pourraient guider les futurs projets de développement au Burkina Faso, en conciliant les impératifs de développement, la protection des populations et la préservation des ressources naturelles. Agence d'information du Burkina BAK/yos

‘Greatest memorial is not stone or bronze’ – Mahama calls for reforms after helicopter crash
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has called on political leaders, public officials and civil servants to embrace integrity, accountability and selfless service, saying the most meaningful way to honour the eight Ghanaians who died in last year’s military helicopter crash is to build a nation where public service is guided by responsibility rather than privilege. Delivering a reflective address at the National Inter-Faith Memorial Service in Accra on Thursday, August 6, President Mahama said the first anniversary of the tragedy should not only be a time of mourning but also a moment for leaders to examine how their decisions affect the lives of those who serve the country. He argued that the legacy of the eight departed public servants should inspire a renewed commitment to ethical leadership and institutional accountability across every level of government. “Today should also be a moment of reflection for all of us who are entrusted with leadership, that every decision we make affects lives,” the President said. He reminded public office holders that leadership carries a moral obligation that extends beyond authority and political power. “Every public office is ultimately a sacred trust. Leadership is not measured merely by the authority we exercise, but by the responsibility we bear for the lives and welfare of those who serve our nation.” President Mahama said the helicopter tragedy underscored the enormous sacrifices made every day by men and women serving the nation, often without public recognition. He stressed that government has a duty not only to acknowledge those sacrifices but also to create working conditions that protect public servants and enable them to perform their responsibilities safely. “Their memory therefore imposes upon us a solemn obligation to build stronger institutions, to strengthen safety standards wherever necessary, to invest in the welfare of our personnel, and to ensure that no lesson from this tragedy will ever be forgotten.” According to the President, strengthening public institutions should become a lasting response to the tragedy, ensuring that future generations of public servants benefit from improved systems and enhanced safety measures. Rather than focusing on monuments or memorial structures, President Mahama said the most enduring legacy would be reforms that improve governance and protect lives. “The greatest memorial we can build is not one made of stone or bronze. It is one that is built through responsible leadership, improved systems and a steadfast commitment to protecting those who dedicate their lives to Ghana.” He said every effort to strengthen accountability, improve operational standards and invest in personnel welfare would honour the memory of those who lost their lives while serving the Republic. The President’s remarks placed institutional reform at the centre of national remembrance, arguing that genuine tribute requires action rather than symbolism alone. President Mahama also reflected on the significance of the inter-faith gathering, describing it as evidence of Ghana’s unity during moments of national sorrow. “My fellow citizens, our faith teaches us that death is not the end,” he said. “Whether we are Christian or Muslim, whether guided by traditional beliefs or by another form of faith, we all hold on to the conviction that every life has a meaning beyond the years we count on it.” He noted that although Ghanaians worship differently, they remain united by shared values of compassion, hope and solidarity. “That is why we have gathered today in an inter-faith service. We come from different traditions, but we lift one prayer. We come with different expressions of worship, but with one shared hope.” President Mahama prayed for God’s mercy upon the departed and for comfort for the bereaved families, while asking for wisdom for the nation. “We pray that the Almighty God, in His infinite mercy, has welcomed our departed brothers into eternal peace. We pray that He continues to comfort every grieving family, and we pray for the wisdom to live lives that are worthy of the opportunities He has granted to us.” The President urged Ghanaians to transform grief into purpose by living according to the values demonstrated by the eight public servants. “As we leave this memorial service today, let us carry with us not only sadness but also a sense of purpose.” He appealed to citizens and public officials alike to make integrity and service the defining principles of national life. “Let us honour the departed by serving our nation with greater integrity. Let us honour them by placing duty above self-interest. Let us honour them by treating one another with greater kindness.” He added that the nation must strive to create an environment in which every Ghanaian feels that his or her contribution to national development is valued. “Let us honour them by building a Ghana where every citizen feels that their service matters and every sacrifice is remembered.” Acknowledging that grief continues to affect many of the bereaved families, President Mahama said the nation has a continuing obligation to remember those who paid the ultimate price in the service of Ghana. “One year has passed. The pain may have softened for some, but it remains raw for others. Our remembrance endures.” He said history would celebrate the victims not because of the tragic circumstances surrounding their deaths but because of the commitment they demonstrated throughout their lives. “The names of these eight faithful servants will forever occupy a special place in the story of our nation, not because of the manner in which they died, but because of the spirit with which they lived and served God and country.” President Mahama urged Ghanaians to ensure that the legacy of the fallen is reflected in everyday actions. He said the strongest tribute the nation can offer is to build a culture of responsible leadership, stronger institutions and public service founded on integrity, compassion and an unwavering commitment to the national interest.

items.description: Lomé, 6 août (ATOP) – Une cérémonie d’invocation des ancêtres s’est déroulée, le jeudi 6 août dans le palais royal du chef canton de Bè. Elle donne le ton aux différentes activités inscrites dans le programme des festivités de « Duneyno Zâ » dans la localité. La cérémonie a été présidée par le chef du canton de Bè, Togbui Adéla Aklassou IV, en présence des chefs quartiers de Bè. Elle a été marquée par un rituel d’invocation des ancêtres de la collectivité et la sortie du tam-tam jumel Atopani, communément appelé « Tam-Tam parlant ». Le chef canton (au milieu) suivant le rituel Cette fête sera observée cette année juqu’au 15 août. Elle permet de célébrer l’identité culturelle, de renforcer la cohésion sociale, de transmettre l’histoire commune aux générations futures et de promouvoir le développement socio-économique à la base. Au programme de cette fête traditionnelle des communautés « Aflao, Bè et Agoènyivé du Grand Lomé », figurent, entre autres, la prière musulmane, un sport de masse, une activité de reboisement, une séance de sensibilisation sur le code routier et protection de l’environnement. Il est également prévu, une conférence-débat sur le thème : « Jeunesse du Grand-Lomé, porte flambeau de la sauvegarde de la célébration de DUNENYO ZA : quelles stratégies pour une implication efficiente de la génération des jeunes aux activités socio-culturelles dans les communautés », démonstration des mets locaux et une formation des jeunes à l’élaboration de plans d’affaires et aux techniques de recherche de financement. items.title: Aviation agencies, airlines clash over 5% levy sharing formula as Minister skips Reps hearing
items.description: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja Nigeria’s aviation agencies and airline operators on Thursday presented competing proposals over the sharing of the statutory five per cent Ticket Sales Charge (TSC), exposing deep divisions over the funding structure of the aviation sector. The disagreement emerged at a public hearing organised by the House of Representatives Committee on Aviation on proposed amendments to the Civil Aviation Act, 2022 and the Nigerian Airspace Management Agency (NAMA) Act. The hearing attracted submissions from aviation regulators, service providers, airline operators and training institutions, with stakeholders seeking changes to the existing revenue-sharing arrangement. However, the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, was absent from the hearing despite the implications of the proposed amendments for agencies under his ministry. While stakeholders agreed on the need for sustainable funding of aviation institutions, they disagreed sharply on how the existing five per cent levy should be distributed. The Nigerian Airspace Management Agency (NAMA) called for an increase in its allocation from 22 per cent to 56 per cent, arguing that the current formula does not reflect the cost of maintaining Nigeria’s airspace infrastructure. Presenting the agency’s position, NAMA Managing Director, Engr. Farouk Ahmed Umar, said the agency currently receives about 1.1 per cent of every qualifying ticket or cargo sale despite being responsible for air traffic management, surveillance systems, communication facilities, navigation aids and other safety-critical infrastructure. “The amendment before you is therefore not merely about dividing revenue. It is about deciding whether the institution entrusted with guiding aircraft will have the stable resources to maintain today’s services and renew tomorrow’s infrastructure,” Umar said. NAMA also requested that the National Assembly recognise obstacle assessment and WGS-84 aeronautical survey as chargeable technical services and allow the agency to retain 90 per cent of the associated fees. The Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA), however, opposed any reduction in its share, insisting that the regulator relies heavily on the Ticket Sales Charge to perform its statutory oversight responsibilities Director-General of Civil Aviation, Capt. Chris Najomo, said although the NCAA supports adequate funding for all aviation agencies, any redistribution must be in line with International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) standards. Najomo argued that NAMA already generates significant commercial revenue from air navigation services, unlike the NCAA. “We submit that NCAA’s allocation of the five per cent Ticket Sales Charge be restored to 65 per cent to overcome the deficiencies identified by ICAO at its last audit and bring Nigeria in line with global best funding practices,” he said. He added that aviation safety depends not only on legislation but also on competent inspectors, effective surveillance, continuous certification, technical training, international cooperation and a financially independent regulator. The African Aviation and Aerospace University (AAAU), Abuja, also joined the debate, demanding recognition as a statutory beneficiary of the levy. The institution argued that as Nigeria’s only specialised aviation university, it should receive not less than 10 per cent of the Ticket Sales Charge to support aviation manpower development, research and innovation. Domestic airline operators, however, argued that the issue should go beyond merely sharing the existing five per cent levy. Speaking on behalf of the Airline Operators of Nigeria (AON), former NAMA Managing Director and aviation expert, Capt. Roland Iyayi, described the current funding model as outdated and burdensome to airlines. “The five per cent service charge has outlived its usefulness. It has created a burden on domestic airlines,” Iyayi said. He disclosed that AON had submitted a comprehensive proposal for institutional reforms in the aviation sector, calling for a complete overhaul of the funding structure rather than simply reallocating the existing revenue. According to him, domestic airlines are facing rising operating costs, with aviation fuel accounting for about 40 per cent of their expenses. Iyayi said airlines have struggled to remit the five per cent charge because a large portion of ticket revenue is consumed by fuel costs. While supporting NAMA’s request for a larger share of the levy, airline operators proposed replacing the percentage-based charge with a unit charge model similar to the passenger service charge collected by the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN). They also called for the establishment of an Aviation Development Fund into which all aviation revenues would be paid before transparent distribution among agencies. The operators further urged lawmakers to remove aviation agencies from the Fiscal Responsibility Commission remittance regime, arguing that surplus revenues should remain within the sector for infrastructure development. They also recommended that obstacle clearance fees currently collected by the NCAA be transferred to NAMA, which performs the technical assessments required for such approvals. Declaring the hearing open on behalf of the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Abbas Tajudeen, Chairman of the House Committee on Aviation, Rep. Abdullahi Idris Garba, said the proposed amendments were aimed at improving transparency, strengthening aviation institutions and enhancing safety. Garba assured stakeholders that all memoranda submitted during the hearing would receive fair consideration before the committee presents its recommendations to the House. The committee is expected to review the competing proposals before deciding whether to amend the revenue-sharing formula governing the aviation industry’s five per cent Ticket Sales Charge. items.title: ‘Grief remains’ – Peter Anala’s family appeals for prayers one year after helicopter crash
items.description: The family of Squadron Leader Peter Bafemi Anala, one of the eight people who lost their lives in the August 6, 2025 military helicopter crash at Adansi Akrofuom in the Ashanti Region, has appealed to Ghanaians to continue praying for the bereaved families, saying the pain of the tragedy remains deeply felt a year on. Delivering the family’s tribute at the National Inter-Faith Memorial Service on Thursday, August 6, 2026, family representative Percy Anala said the passage of time had done little to ease the grief caused by the loss of their loved one. He noted that the late officer’s absence continues to leave a significant void, particularly for his wife, young daughter, mother and the wider family, who are still adjusting to life without him. Despite the difficult year, Percy Anala said the family has drawn strength from God’s grace, as well as the prayers, encouragement and kindness shown by Ghanaians since the tragedy. “We ask you to keep the families of the fallen in your prayers. Though time passes, grief remains. Your ongoing love, encouragement and support are priceless,” he appealed. He also reflected on the family’s painful journey, saying: “Today marks one year since our lives changed forever. Though a year has passed, it feels like yesterday. The loss of our beloved Peter Bafemi Anala remains profoundly painful. “The last year has not been easy. We have faced grief, unanswered questions, and difficult adjustments, especially for his wife, young daughter, mother and the entire family.” The family also remembered the seven other victims who died in the crash, acknowledging that their loved ones continue to endure the same sense of loss. They further expressed gratitude to President John Dramani Mahama and the Government of Ghana for the support extended to the bereaved families, describing the compassion shown over the past year as a source of comfort during an incredibly difficult period.

items.title: Bono East Police shut Kwame-Danso station after attack on officers during court escort
items.description: The Bono East Regional Police Administration has temporarily closed the Kwame-Danso Police Station in the Sene West District after some irate youth allegedly attacked police officers and judicial service personnel. The incident occurred on Wednesday, August 5, 2026, when police officers escorted a suspect to court in Kwame-Danso for judicial proceedings. The attack prompted the temporary closure of the police station as authorities assessed the security situation and took steps to restore order in the area. The police have since restored calm and are engaging relevant stakeholders to ensure normal policing activities resume as soon as possible. Speaking in an interview with the Ghana News Agency (GNA) in Techiman, the Bono East Regional Police Commander, Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCoP) Shaibu Abubakari Sadique-Osei, described the incident as unfortunate and appealed to residents to support the police in maintaining peace and combating crime instead of attacking security personnel. He reaffirmed the Ghana Police Service’s commitment to protecting lives and property, urged residents to remain law-abiding, and disclosed that the Regional Police Command was working closely with the Police Headquarters in Accra to facilitate the reopening of the Kwame-Danso Police Station.

items.title: Football : Kim Gougeon, un ailier burkinabè prometteur trace sa route vers le haut niveau
items.description: À 20 ans, Kim Gougeon s’impose comme l’un des joueurs les plus percutants du championnat corse (France). Entre statistiques solides et ambition débordante, le jeune ailier droit rêve déjà de porter les couleurs du Burkina Faso. Né le 24 février 2006 au Burkina Faso, Kim Gougeon a grandi avec un ballon dans les pieds et une idée fixe. Celle de percer parmi l’élite. Installé aujourd’hui en Corse, ce jeune ailier droit ne cesse de gravir les échelons à une vitesse qui force le respect. Rapide, déterminé et animé d’une ambition rare, il s’est fixé pour objectif d'évoluer au plus haut niveau et, à terme, défendre les couleurs de la sélection nationale burkinabè. Son parcours témoigne d’une progression constante. Après des passages remarqués au Capi Corsu, puis à l’ECB, Kim a posé ses valises au Gallia Club Lucciana, où il évolue désormais en Régional 1. Un palier de plus franchi avec autorité pour ce jeune joueur dont les statistiques plaident en sa faveur. Depuis le début de la saison 2025-2026, il totalise quatorze matchs disputés, dont treize en tant que titulaire, pour six buts inscrits et quatre passes décisives délivrées. Ce qui fait la force de Kim Gougeon, c’est d’abord une palette technique complète. Sa vitesse et sa percussion sur le côté droit en font un adversaire redoutable pour les défenses. Son dribble, ses appels de balle et sa finition devant le but sont autant d’atouts qui lui permettent de faire la différence. Mais au-delà du talent individuel, c’est son esprit d’équipe qui séduit. Jamais avare d’efforts, il travaille aussi pour ses coéquipiers et participe pleinement au collectif. Avec une mentalité de compétiteur et un potentiel encore à exploiter, Kim Gougeon semble armé pour écrire les prochaines belles pages de sa jeune carrière. items.title: Richard Ahiagbah explains NPP Democracy Under Attack protest, calls for fairness in state investigations
items.description: The Director of Communications for the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Richard Ahiagbah, has described the party’s “Democracy Under Attack” demonstration as a legitimate expression of concern over what it believes is the selective application of justice and the alleged targeting of opposition members by state institutions. According to him, the protest was organised to draw national attention to issues the party considers critical to the protection of the rule of law, fairness and the independence of state investigative bodies. Mr Ahiagbah maintained that the NPP was not opposed to the work of institutions such as the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO), but insisted that they must carry out their constitutional responsibilities impartially and professionally. He also appealed to EOCO’s Executive Director, Raymond Archer, to ensure that investigations are conducted without bias and in a manner that inspires public confidence. Speaking to Channel One TV during Thursday’s demonstration, Mr Ahiagbah said: “Raymond Archer is doing his work, but he must do it professionally. We don’t have any intention of gagging state institutions. What we are saying is that they must do their work professionally and nobody will complain if they do their work professionally. “What is being done today may be repeated tomorrow if they are not mindful. What we need is that everyone should be treated fairly, and we are not asking for special treatment, so the selectivity must stop. We are all Ghanaians and the NDC must govern the country for the benefit of all Ghanaians.” The “Democracy Under Attack” demonstration attracted hundreds of NPP supporters, party executives and sympathisers, who marched through the principal streets of Accra after assembling at the forecourt of the Supreme Court. The protesters are expected to present petitions to the judiciary and the Presidency as part of their demands for what they describe as greater fairness and respect for democratic principles.

items.title: 'Growing pattern of media curbs': HRCP, PFUJ express concern over new rules for foreign press
items.description: The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) and the Pakistan Federal Union of Journalists (PFUJ) have expressed concerns regarding media freedom after the government mandated foreign media personnel to seek permission for travelling to any city outside Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi for news coverage. “The requirement that journalists obtain state approval to report from large parts of the country sends a chilling message: that critical reporting is unwelcome,” HRCP noted in a statement on Wednesday about the ‘Foreign Media Facilitation Guidelines 2026’. Expressing its deep concern, the commission said the rules would “invariably institutionalise bureaucratic control over news gathering and risk deterring independent reporting on matters of public interest” rather than facilitate journalism. “This is the latest in a growing pattern of restrictions on media freedom in Pakistan. From arbitrary curbs on reporting and increasing censorship to legal and administrative barriers, the space for independent journalism has continued to shrink,” the rights body highlighted. It urged the government to withdraw the “restrictive measures and uphold its constitutional and international obligation to protect freedom of expression”. Similarly, PFUJ “strongly condemned” the new rules and termed them as restrictions on press freedom. In a statement issued on Thursday, PFUJ President Afzal Butt and Secretary General Arshad Ansari said the guidelines amount to “attacking the freedom of expression and putting curbs on press freedom”. “The government has not only banned foreign journalists from visiting most of the areas of Pakistan except major cities, but they have also restricted the movement of Pakistani media persons working with international media outlets. They are not allowed to visit these areas on their own either,” it pointed out. “How can foreign correspondents and their Pakistani colleagues perform their professional duties after this notification?” the PFUJ leaders asked. They further asserted that the move would “only bring disrepute to Pakistan and damage its image”. The PFUJ statement noted, “Pakistan is already ranked very low among the countries that have the worst record in press freedom. And the action of the government would add to it.” It demanded that the government immediately “lift this ban” if it believed in democracy and press freedom, arguing that such a move would also impact the employment of Pakistanis working with international media outlets. “Naturally, if Pakistani journalists working with global media outlets are unable to visit different areas, it means they would not be able to perform their professional responsibilities. Consequently, they would lose their jobs,” it contended. The PFUJ leaders were quoted as saying that such actions “are taken in banana republics, not in countries that claim to follow democratic principles”. “If the demands of PFUJ are not accepted, we would be left with no option but to resort to protest and demonstrations,” it warned. In a post on X, Amnesty International also urged “Pakistan’s authorities to end the escalating restrictions on the right to freedom of expression, including press freedom, access to information, and human rights advocacy”. In a letter addressed to the government, Amnesty, HRCP and others called for the withdrawal of the Foreign Media Facilitation Guidelines 2026, which they said placed “onerous restrictions on reporting by foreign journalists”. According to the new guidelines, all foreign media personnel will now need a no-objection certificate (NOC) from the information ministry to travel to any city except Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi to produce “news content, story, video, film, documentary or social media content” for official use. Additionally, under the new rules, all entities operating in Pakistan to facilitate foreign media “in any capacity” are also required to register with the ministry’s External Publicity (EP) Wing, as are non-journalists living in Pakistan who render services to foreign media. The guidelines also specify that individuals’ press registration can be suspended or withdrawn for “acts against ideology, sovereignty, security or public order of Pakistan”, and if the EP Wing “deems appropriate at any stage”.

items.title: Dunenyo-za / Une cérémonie de libation marque le lancement de la huitième édition
items.description: Agoè-Nyivé, 6 août (ATOP) – La huitième édition de la fête traditionnelle Dunenyo-Za a été lancée, le jeudi 6 août à Legbassito, par une cérémonie de libation destinée à solliciter la bénédiction et la protection des mânes des ancêtres pour la réussite des festivités. La cérémonie a réuni autour du chef canton de Legbassito, Togbui Agbotro-Logbo Koami Djidjoli IV, le président cantonal de l’Union des communautés d’Agoè-Nyivé pour le développement (UCAD), Gbingli Komlan, des chefs traditionnels, des prêtres coutumiers, des Assafo, ainsi que des autorités administratives et politiques. A travers les rites de libation, la communauté a confié aux ancêtres l’ensemble des activités de cette édition, placée sous le thème, « Avec Dunenyo-Za, valorisons la jeunesse et la femme, acteurs du développement durable ». Plusieurs activités sont inscrites au programme, notamment des prières musulmanes, un tournoi de football, des jeux ludiques, des consultations foraines, une dictée en éwé, des démonstrations d’Avodada et d’Abo, une formation des jeunes en entrepreneuriat et une journée dédiée aux femmes. L’apothéose de la huitième édition est prévue le 15 août au stade communal d’Adéwi-Anyigbé (Franciscains). Pour le chef canton de Legbassito, la huitième édition de la fête communautaire est dédiée particulièrement à la célébration de la femme et de la jeunesse ; leur valorisation, leur promotion et leur contribution au développement durable. “La gent féminine et surtout la jeunesse du Grand Lomé, relève de demain, ont le devoir de s’approprier et de pérenniser les valeurs de Dunenyo-Za. La survie de notre identité culturelle doit être conservée et transmise de génération en génération », a-t-il souligné. Dunenyo-Za est une manifestation culturelle qui rassemble les fils et filles des communautés de Bè, d’Aflao et d’Agoè-Nyivé (Grand Lomé) autour de leur patrimoine culturel et de leurs valeurs traditionnelles. ATOP/MG/

États-Unis : pourquoi la victoire d’Abdul El-Sayed au Michigan est une mauvaise nouvelle pour le Maroc
items.description: Les lignes bougent dans la politique intérieure américaine et bougeront probablement dans la géopolitique mondiale, ce qui constitue une mauvaise nouvelle pour l’axe Maroc–Israël. La victoire du démocrate d'origine égyptienne Abdul El-Sayed dans une primaire démocrate n’est pas un événement anodin. Après l’élection de Zohran Mamdani à la tête de la mairie de New York en novembre dernier, elle constitue un autre symptôme qu’un vent de changement est en train de traverser la société américaine. Pour Donald Trump, Israël et ses alliés, dont notamment le Maroc, c’est tout sauf une bonne nouvelle. Abdul El-Sayed gagne face à l'argent des lobbies pro-israéliens Abdul El-Sayed, médecin musulman de 41 ans d'origine égyptienne, a remporté mercredi 5 août la primaire démocrate du Michigan pour l’élection sénatoriale de novembre prochain. Il est vrai que ce n'est pas toutes les semaines qu’un musulman remporte un scrutin aux États-Unis, mais la victoire d’El-Sayed marque les esprits pour d’autres raisons. Le scrutin est, en effet, perçu comme un référendum miniature pour ou contre Donald Trump, pour ou contre la poursuite du soutien inconditionnel à Israël et ses crimes contre les Palestiniens. La campagne du vote a été très marquée par la question du rapport à Israël. Des dizaines de millions de dollars ont été dépensés par le lobby pro-israéliens pour faire barrage à El Sayed, qui disposait de huit fois moins de financements, et faire élire Haley Stevens, faisant de cette campagne la plus onéreuse de l'histoire pour une primaire sénatoriale, selon les analystes politiques américains. L'AIPAC, la puissante organisation américaine pro-israélienne, a mis à elle seule 32 millions de dollars. El-Sayed a répliqué qu'elle « peut brûler son argent ». Une autre bête noire de Netanyahou La victoire du médecin d’origine égyptienne est aussi importante, car elle confirme une tendance entamée avec l'élection de Zohran Mamdani, un autre musulman, comme maire de New York en novembre dernier, lui aussi contre un candidat soutenu par le monde de la finance. Depuis son entrée en fonction en janvier dernier, Mamdani est devenu la bête noire de Donald Trump et de Benyamin Netanyahou, qu’il a menacé de faire arrêter s’il se rend à New York pour l’assemblée générale de l’ONU. Abdul El-Sayed est sur la même ligne. Il plaide pour la fin de l'aide américaine à Israël, critique l'influence de l’Aipac dans les élections à tous les niveaux et s’oppose à l'existence d'Israël comme un État uniquement réservé aux Juifs. El-Sayed n’est pas encore sénateur, il devra pour le devenir battre en novembre prochain le candidat républicain Mike Rogers. Mais la symbolique de sa victoire aux primaires sème déjà un vent de panique chez ses adversaires, jusqu'en Israël. Elle confirme le retournement progressif de l'électorat démocrate sur la question du soutien à Israël. Barack Obama l'avait prédit il y a plusieurs années et Benyamin Netanyahou a accéléré le processus avec son génocide à Gaza. Vance : « Qu’à Dieu ne plaise, il pourrait devenir président… » La panique se lit à travers les réactions à la victoire de Abdul El-Sayed. Donald Trump l’a qualifié de « communiste raté qui déteste les Juifs et Israël ». Le vice-président DJ Vance a même évoqué le scénario de voir le médecin d’origine égyptienne devenir président des États-Unis. « Qu’à Dieu ne plaise, Abdul El-Sayed pourrait devenir président dans trois ans. Nous ne voulons pas qu'il remette en cause tout ce que nous avons fait pour faire tomber les escrocs et préserver l'argent du peuple américain », a dit Vance. Voir cette publication sur Instagram Une publication partagée par الجزيرة – مصر (@aja.egypt) Zohran Mamdani a souligné particulièrement la victoire d’El-Sayed face aux forces de l'argent pro-israéliennes. « Malgré plus de 60 millions de dollars de dépenses indépendantes engagées contre lui, il a réussi à l’emporter (…) Je suis fier de faire partie d'un mouvement d'élus et de candidats qui veulent remettre les Américains de la classe ouvrière au cœur de notre vie politique », a réagi le maire de New York. Pas une bonne nouvelle pour Israël et le Maroc En France, Bally Bagayoko, élu maire de Saint-Denis en mars dernier, a estimé que « le vent de la rupture souffle » et a salué une génération qui affirme « son soutien aux droits du peuple palestinien, condamne les politiques du gouvernement israélien qu’elle juge contraires au droit international et plaide pour une paix fondée sur la justice, l’égalité des droits et le respect de la dignité de tous ». Un vent de rupture souffle sur la gauche américaine ! Les lignes bougent. Après la victoire de Zohran Mamdani à New York, Abdul El-Sayed remporte à son tour la primaire démocrate pour l’élection sénatoriale dans le Michigan, porté par le soutien de Bernie Sanders, Elizabeth… pic.twitter.com/xrcOUCd5Hh — Bally Bagayoko (@BallyBagayoko) August 5, 2026 Outre Israël, ce vent de changement inquiète également tous ceux qui, à travers le monde, ont tout misé sur la protection de Donald Trump et d’Israël. C’est particulièrement le cas du Maroc qui vient de baptiser une autoroute du nom du président américain qui a reconnu en 2020 la « souveraineté marocaine » sur le Sahara occidental en contrepartie de la normalisation des relations du royaume avec Israël. Devenu un pays de l’Internationale réactionnaire, le Maroc devrait peut-être songer à cesser de bomber le torse et de lâcher ses bombes migratoires sur ses voisins européens. L’article États-Unis : pourquoi la victoire d'Abdul El-Sayed au Michigan est une mauvaise nouvelle pour le Maroc est apparu en premier sur TSA .
